46:T112f,## Scope

`NON_REAL_EVIDENCE_RE` in `scripts/check-pr-evidence.mjs` voids a whole evidence block when a fabrication marker appears anywhere inside it, including as part of an identifier. A genuine transcript that merely *names* a command or file containing one of those words is classified as fake evidence and the row reports `blank`.

The trigger is a real one from this repo:

```js
const NON_REAL_EVIDENCE_RE =
  /\b(?:placeholder|example output|logs? here|todo|tbd|fabricated|invented|fake|mocks?|fixtures?|synthetic|dummy)\b/i;

NON_REAL_EVIDENCE_RE.test("$ bun run audit:test-integrity:no-vi-mocks");   // true
NON_REAL_EVIDENCE_RE.test("packages/scripts/lint-no-vi-mocks.mjs:12");     // true
NON_REAL_EVIDENCE_RE.test("running fixtures/setup.ts");                    // true
```

`\b` matches after a hyphen and after a slash, so `no-vi-mocks` and `fixtures/setup.ts` both trip it. Any PR pasting real output from that lint — or from anything under a `fixtures/` path — has its evidence row rejected as fabricated.

I hit this while filling the evidence rows on #17591: the honest transcript quoted `audit:test-integrity:no-vi-mocks`, so the gate marked the row `blank`. I shipped that PR with one word redacted and a note explaining why, which is precisely the wrong incentive — the gate pushed real evidence out of the PR.

## Proposed fix

Require the marker to stand alone rather than appear inside a hyphenated or slashed identifier:

```js
const NON_REAL_EVIDENCE_RE =
  /(?<![\w\/-])(?:placeholder|example output|logs? here|todo|tbd|fabricated|invented|fake|mocks?|fixtures?|synthetic|dummy)(?![\w\/-])/i;
```

Verified against both directions — real evidence must pass, genuine fabrication must still be caught:

| Input | Current | Proposed | Wanted |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$ bun run audit:test-integrity:no-vi-mocks` | flagged | passes | passes |
| `packages/scripts/lint-no-vi-mocks.mjs:12` | flagged | passes | passes |
| `running fixtures/setup.ts` | flagged | passes | passes |
| `TODO: logs here` | flagged | flagged | flagged |
| `this is a placeholder` | flagged | flagged | flagged |
| `output was fabricated` | flagged | flagged | flagged |
| `uses mocks instead of the real service` | flagged | flagged | flagged |

The last row matters: the point of `mocks`/`fixtures` in this pattern is to reject evidence produced by a mocked test, per the repo's "no larp" standard. That intent is preserved — a bare `mocks` in prose is still caught. Only occurrences welded into an identifier stop matching.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A transcript quoting a command or path containing a marker word (`no-vi-mocks`, `fixtures/…`) satisfies the gate when it otherwise meets the inline-transcript floor.
- [ ] Genuine fabrication markers still void the block: bare `placeholder`, `TODO`, `logs here`, `fabricated`, and a prose disclosure such as "uses mocks instead of the real service".
- [ ] `runSelfTest` covers both directions, so a future tightening cannot silently reintroduce the false positive.
- [ ] No other change to what the gate accepts.

## Evidence plan

- [ ] Screenshots / video: N/A - CI script change with no rendered surface.
- [ ] Logs: before/after classification for the table above, pasted inline.
- [ ] Real-LLM trajectories: N/A - no model, prompt, action, or provider behavior changes.
- [ ] Domain artifacts: N/A - the self-test result is the artifact.
- [ ] Commands: `node scripts/check-pr-evidence.mjs --self-test`, `node --test scripts/check-pr-evidence.test.mjs`.

This issue is deliberately separate because it *does* change what the gate accepts, and I did not want to widen a PR whose stated scope excluded that. Happy to sequence them in whichever order you prefer.

<!-- eliza-computer-attribution:v1 {"provider":"openai","model":"gpt-5.6-sol","client":"Codex desktop","skill_revision":"elizaOS/eliza@04ff8982861e7aa5045c0a065fb7e1d8750e6e6b:packages/skills/skills/contribute-to-eliza"} -->4a:Td8b,## What is wrong

`agent_sandboxes_lifecycle_revision_trigger` fires on **every** update to the table:

```sql
CREATE TRIGGER agent_sandboxes_lifecycle_revision_trigger
BEFORE UPDATE ON "agent_sandboxes"
FOR EACH ROW
EXECUTE FUNCTION advance_agent_sandbox_lifecycle_revision();
```

No `WHEN` clause. That is what makes the revision unforgeable — a raw SQL writer cannot dodge it — and inside a single transaction it is exactly right.

**Across two transactions it means something weaker than the code assumes.** `lifecycle_revision = $expected` reads as *"did a lifecycle operation intervene?"*, but what it actually asserts is *"did anything at all touch this row?"*. Those are the same statement only if every writer to the table is a lifecycle operation, and several are not.

## The writers that are not lifecycle operations

| writer | columns it sets |
|---|---|
| `lib/services/active-billing.ts` | `billing_status`, `scheduled_shutdown_at`, `shutdown_warning_sent_at`, `updated_at` |
| `db/repositories/agent-billing.ts` | `billing_status`, `hourly_rate`, `last_billed_at`, `scheduled_shutdown_at`, `shutdown_warning_sent_at` |

The `active-billing` suspension write runs on a periodic cycle, outside the lifecycle advisory lock, gated only on `deletion_attempt_id IS NULL` — **not** on status. A row in `provisioning` is therefore reachable.

## The failure

`revokeWarmClaimSourceCredential` reads the revision in one transaction, performs out-of-band credential work, then re-fences in a second. On a miss it does not retry — `eliza-sandbox.ts` throws `Warm-claim credential finalization lost its state CAS`, which is terminal.

So a billing-cycle write landing in that window converts a **successful** warm claim into a hard provisioning failure. The window is however long the credential work takes, and the trigger for it is a periodic job that has nothing to do with the agent's lifecycle. The same broadening applies to the replacement-cleanup fences, which span docker and VPN I/O and so hold the window open for seconds.

Before the revision fence those CASes were scoped to `status` / `warm_claim_*` / `environment_revision`, all immune to a billing write. This is a regression introduced with the fence, in #17262, which I wrote.

## Fix

Narrow the trigger with a `WHEN` clause so the revision advances only when a column some CAS actually fences on changes value. That keeps the property that matters — a lifecycle write cannot dodge the counter, whatever statement performs it — while a billing write stops looking like a lifecycle event.

The column list has to be a **superset** of everything any fence reads, because under-listing reintroduces the ABA window the fence exists to close, which is worse than the current bug. So the list gets derived from the code and pinned by a test that fails when a new fenced column appears without being added to the trigger — a drift guard, not a comment asking people to remember.

Two alternatives considered and not taken: routing the billing writers through the lifecycle advisory lock couples billing to lifecycle contention for no benefit; making each call site retry turns a correctness bug into a latency bug and leaves the predicate lying.

## Not reachable from

Same-transaction fences are unaffected — the trigger still fires for them and the read cannot be stale. Only cross-transaction fences are exposed.

Found by @ss251 while reviewing #17262. Refs #17262 [stan-cloud]

- Project board: N/A — tooling defect in `packages/scripts`.
- Parent tracker or epic: relates to the live-test artifact-coverage gate described in `packages/scenario-runner/docs/coding-capability-audit/MASTER_PLAN.md:103`.
- Coordination Discussion: N/A.
- Suggested lane tag: claude-code-ss251

## Scope

**`check-live-test-artifact-coverage.mjs` shells out to `rg` without declaring it as a dependency, and reports its absence as a repository-listing failure — so an operator without ripgrep is told the wrong thing.**

`packages/scripts/check-live-test-artifact-coverage.mjs:149-157`:

```js
function packageJsonPaths() {
  const completed = spawnSync("rg", ["--files", "-g", "package.json"], {
    cwd: REPO_ROOT,
    encoding: "utf8",
    stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
  });
  if (completed.status !== 0) {
    throw new Error(completed.stderr || "failed to list package.json files");
  }
```

When `rg` is not on PATH, `spawnSync` does not fail the way this code assumes:

- `completed.status` is **`null`**, not a nonzero exit code — `null !== 0` is true, so the branch is taken for the right reason by accident
- `completed.error.code` is **`ENOENT`** — and `completed.error` is never inspected
- `completed.stderr` is **`undefined`**, not the child's stderr, because no child ever ran

so `completed.stderr || "failed to list package.json files"` falls through to the generic message. The operator is told the repository could not be listed when the actual cause is a missing binary.

Reproduced directly (same `spawnSync` shape, absent binary):

```
$ node -e "const {spawnSync}=require('node:child_process');
  const c=spawnSync('definitely-not-a-real-binary-xyz',['--files'],{encoding:'utf8',stdio:['ignore','pipe','pipe']});
  console.log('status:',JSON.stringify(c.status));
  console.log('error.code:',c.error&&c.error.code);
  console.log('stderr:',JSON.stringify(c.stderr));
  console.log('=> the checker throws:',JSON.stringify(c.stderr||'failed to list package.json files'));"
status: null
error.code: ENOENT
stderr: undefined
=> the checker throws: "failed to list package.json files"
```

### Why this one is easy to miss

`rg` is an undeclared dependency here, and this is the **only** `spawnSync("rg", …)` site under `packages/scripts` and `scripts` (`git grep`, 1 hit). The repo is otherwise explicit that ripgrep must be provisioned where it is required:

- `.github/workflows/build-linux-iso.yml:75` — *"ripgrep (rg) is a hard dependency of `packages/os/linux/scripts/static-smoke.sh`"*
- `.github/workflows/elizaos-os-release.yml:87-108` — downloads it from GitHub releases

This script has no such provisioning step, and no CI lane currently invokes it — it is referenced only from `MASTER_PLAN.md`, which plans to *extend it to fail coding/orchestrator PRs lacking an evidence bundle*. So the masking is harmless today and becomes a confusing CI failure exactly when the gate is turned on.

## Proposed Fix

Either fix is small; they are independent and both are repo-idiomatic.

1. **Remove the undeclared dependency.** List tracked files with git, as the repo's other checkers do:
   ```js
   const completed = spawnSync("git", ["ls-files", "*package.json"], { cwd: REPO_ROOT, encoding: "utf8" });
   ```
   git is already a hard requirement everywhere this runs, and `ls-files` respects tracking rather than `.gitignore` heuristics.

2. **Stop masking the cause.** Inspect `completed.error` before `completed.status`, so an ENOENT names the missing binary:
   ```js
   if (completed.error) {
     throw new Error(
       completed.error.code === "ENOENT"
         ? "ripgrep (rg) is required but was not found on PATH"
         : `failed to list package.json files: ${completed.error.message}`,
     );
   }
   ```

Happy to implement either or both if wanted.

50:T1888,## Project / Coordination

- Project board: N/A — release-gate integrity in `packages/app-core`.
- Parent tracker or epic: N/A.
- Coordination Discussion: N/A.
- Suggested lane tag: claude-code-ss251

## Scope

**`release-check.ts`'s macOS artifact-stager gate cannot detect the regression it exists to prevent: deleting the `exit 1` that fails a required-staple release leaves the gate reporting PASS.**

`assertMacArtifactStagerLooksCorrect` (`packages/app-core/scripts/release-check.ts:1025-1085`) guards `packages/app-core/platforms/electrobun/scripts/stage-macos-release-artifacts.sh` by transcribing one contiguous 9-line block of that script (lines 483-493) into **41 independent substring assertions**, each tested with `script.includes(snippet)` in isolation.

Three of those 41 are bare shell punctuation, and they are not rare in the guarded file:

| asserted literal | occurrences in `stage-macos-release-artifacts.sh` |
| --- | --- |
| `"    exit 1"` | 9 |
| `"  fi"` | 26 |
| `"fi"` | 58 |

Because each literal is tested alone, the gate asserts only that every line exists **somewhere in the file, in any order, at any distance**. It never pins adjacency, order, or nesting — and the block's entire semantic payload happens to live in one of the vacuous literals.

The behaviour being guarded is the release's fail-hard contract, `stage-macos-release-artifacts.sh:485-490`:

```sh
if ! retry_command "$STAPLER_ATTEMPTS" "$STAPLER_DELAY_SECONDS" xcrun stapler staple "$TEMP_DMG_PATH"; then
  if [[ "${ELECTROBUN_REQUIRE_STAPLED_DMG:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "stage-macos-release-artifacts: notarization accepted but stapler ticket was not available; continuing without stapled DMG" >&2
fi
```

Delete line 487 (`exit 1`) and a release that **requires** a stapled DMG stops failing — it falls through to the warning and silently ships an unstapled DMG. `release-check` stays green, because `exit 1` still matches nine other places in the file.

## Evidence

Mutation probe run against `origin/develop@e9d64249f`. The probe parses the checker's `requiredSnippets`/`forbiddenSnippets` arrays **out of `release-check.ts`'s own source** rather than retyping them — a retyped probe tests the transcription, not the checker — then re-runs the gate's exact predicate against mutated copies of the stager:

```
checker asserts 41 required + 2 forbidden literals about
  packages/app-core/platforms/electrobun/scripts/stage-macos-release-artifacts.sh (498 lines)

BASELINE (unmutated)  : release-check snippet gate => PASS (missing 0)

MUTANT A: deleted line 487 ("      exit 1") — required-staple release no longer fails
MUTANT A              : release-check snippet gate => PASS (missing 0)

MUTANT B: deleted lines 486-488 (the entire ELECTROBUN_REQUIRE_STAPLED_DMG guard)
MUTANT B              : release-check snippet gate => FAIL (missing 1: ["  if [[ \"${ELECTROBUN_REQUIRE_STAPLED_DMG:-0}\" == \"1\" ]]; then"])

=> guard detects mutant A: NO (escapes)
=> guard detects mutant B: yes
```

Mutant B is caught only because the distinctive condition line disappears. So the gate pins **the presence of the condition**, never **the behaviour under it** — which is the half that matters.

To be explicit about what this is not: the tree currently satisfies all 41 literals, and `ELECTROBUN_REQUIRE_STAPLED_DMG` is opt-in (default `0`). This is a **latent guard defect**, not a live release failure — the gate will not notice if the contract is removed later.

## Proposed Fix

Assert the transcribed block as **one multi-line string** instead of N independent lines:

```ts
const requiredStaplerBlock = [
  'if ! retry_command "$STAPLER_ATTEMPTS" "$STAPLER_DELAY_SECONDS" xcrun stapler staple "$TEMP_DMG_PATH"; then',
  '    if [[ "${ELECTROBUN_REQUIRE_STAPLED_DMG:-0}" == "1" ]]; then',
  "      exit 1",
  "    fi",
  // ...
].join("\n");
if (!script.includes(requiredStaplerBlock)) { /* fail */ }
```

Order, adjacency and indentation then come along for free, and every line becomes load-bearing — including the `exit 1`. The same treatment applies to the other contiguous runs in the array (the notarytool submit/wait blocks have the same shape). Literals that cannot discriminate should be dropped rather than left as decoration, since a passing assertion that cannot fail is indistinguishable from an absent one.

Happy to implement this if it is wanted as a contribution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Deleting `exit 1` from the `ELECTROBUN_REQUIRE_STAPLED_DMG` branch of `stage-macos-release-artifacts.sh` makes `release-check`'s stager assertion FAIL.
- [ ] Reordering two lines of the guarded block (without deleting any) makes the assertion FAIL.
- [ ] The unmodified stager at `develop` still PASSES.
- [ ] No asserted literal in `assertMacArtifactStagerLooksCorrect` matches more than one location in the guarded script.

- [ ] CI or local commands: the mutation probe, plus `bun run release:check` on an unmodified tree to show no regression.

51:T778,## What happens

Every deploy of the cloud Worker strands the webhook gateway's JWT until the gateway's next scheduled refresh — up to ~48 minutes (refresh at 80% of the 3600s TTL). Every cloud call the gateway makes in that window fails 401, and those calls run in the post-ack background phase, so each failure is a silent dropped message for a real user.

Observed on production, 2026-08-07:

```
23:56:58  gateway: JWT token refreshed (expiresIn 3600s)   <- signed against the OLD Worker
~00:00    prod Worker redeployed (run 31125155708)
00:03:32  [ERRO] Background message processing failed
          messageId="919799294" error="Identity resolve failed: 401"
00:05:59  manual gateway restart -> fresh bootstrap -> everything works
```

A freshly bootstrapped token against the new Worker resolved the same identity with 200 — verified directly. So the token endpoint and the Worker were healthy the whole time; only the cached token was stale.

## Why

`auth.ts` recovers from a **failed refresh** by re-acquiring (`refreshToken` falls back to `acquireToken`), but nothing reacts to a 401 on a **data call**. `getAuthHeader()` is synchronous and trusts the cached token; `resolveIdentity`, `resolveWebhookConfig` and `sendOnboardingReply` all treat 401 as a terminal error.

## Fix

`reacquireAuthHeader()` in `auth.ts` — a single-flight re-bootstrap returning a fresh header (a Worker deploy 401s every in-flight message at once; without the latch, N messages race N bootstraps against the token endpoint). The three call sites retry exactly once with the fresh header on a 401; a second 401 follows today's error path, and a 404 never triggers a re-bootstrap. The onboarding retry is replay-safe because the call already carries `Idempotency-Key: <messageId>`.

Note: this service deploys via manual `railway up` from the repo root; the fix protects production only after the next gateway deploy.

`packages/cloud/services/gateway-webhook` cannot be built. Reproduced by running the Dockerfile's own deps step against the service directory:

```
$ bun install --frozen-lockfile --production      # with only package.json, as the Dockerfile does
error: Workspace dependency "@elizaos/cloud-services-common" not found
error: @elizaos/cloud-services-common@workspace:* failed to resolve
```

The Dockerfile builds from the service directory:

```dockerfile
COPY package.json ./
RUN bun install --frozen-lockfile --production
```

`workspace:*` has nothing to resolve against in a context that contains only this package.

## When it broke

`a07084e9cbc` (2026-06-28) added `@elizaos/cloud-services-common` to the service's dependencies. Every build since has failed.

Two things hid it:

1. **Nothing builds this service.** It has no repo trigger on Railway (`repoTriggers: NONE`, `source: null`), and `cloud-gateway-webhook.yml` has a single `test` job. The workflow header on the sibling service says *"Railway auto-deploys on push to the watched branch"* — that is not connected for any of these services.
2. **The service ships its own `bun.lock`, and it is stale.** It has no entry for the workspace dependency and pins `hono@4.12.18` while `package.json` asks for `4.12.34`. The root lockfile has both right. So `--frozen-lockfile` was reading a lockfile written before the dependency existed.

## What it cost

The production image dates from **2026-05-14** — the last build that could succeed. Everything since is a redeploy of that image. The running container still logs the pre-#17746 error string, which is how this was found:

```
[ERRO] Background message processing failed
       error="Identity resolve response missing userId, organizationId, or agentId"
```

So #17746 and #17764 — both merged, both fixing connector onboarding for every linked user — have never run in production. Nothing reported this: tests, typecheck and lint all pass, because none of them builds the image.

## Scope: this is a class, not one service

| service | workspace deps | last successful build |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway-webhook` | 1 | 2026-05-14 |
| `gateway-discord` | 1 | 2026-06-19 |
| `agent-server` | 6 | 2026-05-15 |

All three have the same `COPY package.json ./` shape. `gateway-discord` also carries a stale local lockfile.

## Fix

Build from the repository root and write a pruned workspace root in the deps stage — only the service and the packages it needs — so the workspace link resolves without installing the whole monorepo. Measured: 32 packages, 1.5s.

Guarded by a test that derives, for every service with a `workspace:*` dependency, whether its Dockerfile copies that package. The two services still broken are listed explicitly rather than skipped, so fixing one fails the test until the list is updated.

Not covered here: nothing yet guards the deploy half — a service can still go months without a successful build and no signal. Worth a separate check.
53:T8a5,## What happens

Meta cannot register the WhatsApp callback URL. Measured against production on 2026-08-05:

```
GET https://api.elizacloud.ai/api/eliza-app/webhook/whatsapp?hub.mode=subscribe&hub.verify_token=<token>&hub.challenge=PROBE123
→ 401 {"success":false,"code":"WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_INVALID","error":"Invalid webhook signature"}
```

Expected is `200` with the body `PROBE123`.

## Why

Meta verifies a callback URL with a `GET` carrying `hub.mode=subscribe`, `hub.verify_token` and `hub.challenge`, **and no signature header** — there is no body to sign. That is the documented handshake.

`forwardToWebhookGateway` runs `validateLocalWebhookSignature` on every request regardless of method. For a GET, `needsBody` is false, so the body is `""`, and `verifyWhatsAppSignature` returns `false` the moment `x-hub-signature-256` is absent. Meta's challenge is refused before it is read.

The gateway on the other side already implements the handshake correctly — `GET /webhook/:project/whatsapp[/:agentId]` compares `hub.verify_token` and echoes `hub.challenge` — but Meta hits the Worker URL, so it never gets there.

## Why it matters beyond WhatsApp

There are two independent WhatsApp failures in production and they have a mandatory order. The access token has been expired since 2026-02-09 (`Session has expired on Monday, 09-Feb-26 09:00:00 PST`), but regenerating it changes nothing while the URL cannot be registered. This bug is first.

Current state: `SELECT count(*) FROM user_identities WHERE whatsapp_id IS NOT NULL` → **0**. No WhatsApp user has ever existed.

## Fix

Skip the body-signature check for exactly that handshake — WhatsApp platform, `GET`, `hub.mode=subscribe`, `hub.challenge` present — and let it proxy to the gateway, which validates the verify token. The HMAC check on an empty body proves nothing; the verify token is the credential Meta's design uses for this step. Every other WhatsApp request, including every POST, keeps the signature requirement.

## Related

The same audit found that Twilio and blooio share the symptom (`phone_message_log` empty since forever) but their configuration lives with other providers and has not been audited. Separate work.

## Scope

**`bindScheduledTaskToInboundChat` classifies message provenance with two inline string literals, so 3 of the 5 internal sources `@elizaos/core` defines fall through the guard and are bound to outbound connector dispatch — the exact failure d4b58b496 exists to prevent.**

`plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/src/lifeops/scheduled-task/delivery-binding.ts` (at `develop@f7ad1a740`) gates the binding twice, and both gates are denylists:

```ts
// :71-76 — the inbound envelope
const inboundSource =
  stringField(message.metadata?.source) ?? stringField(message.content.source);
if (inboundSource === "api" || inboundSource === "client_chat") {
  return null;
}
// :78-86 — the resolved room
const source = stringField(room?.source);
if (source === "api" || source === "client_chat" || channelId === room.id) {
  return null;
}
```

A denylist here is **fail-open**: a provenance the list does not name falls through into the binding. The commit message states what falls through means — internal turns "are rewritten into unavailable outbound connector sends and planner idempotency keys leak a synthetic room suffix."

### The list is short against the repo's own canonical list

`packages/core/src/types/message-source.ts` is the canonical module for exactly this classification, and its docstring says why it exists:

> Well-known `source` sentinels for messages the agent originates or routes internally (client chat, sub-agent, coding-agent, agent greeting), **so routing and gating code can branch on provenance without magic strings.**

It names five: `client_chat`, `sub_agent`, `coding-agent`, `agent_greeting`, `trigger-prompt`. The new guard covers **one** of them, plus `"api"`, which the module does not define at all.

The same package already treats one of the missing three as a peer of the two that are covered, in this precise reject-a-connector-shaped-internal-turn role — `src/lifeops/family-communications/production-wiring.pglite.integration.test.ts:377`:

```ts
it.each(["client_chat", "api", "sub_agent"])(
  "rejects the %s provider even when connector-like metadata is present",
  ...
```

That test name is the whole issue in one line: the established in-repo standard is that `sub_agent` must be rejected *even when the surrounding metadata looks like a connector*. The new guard implements two thirds of that triad.

### `sub_agent` reaches this call path in a real connector room

The uncovered state is constructible from the tree, end to end:

1. `plugins/plugin-agent-orchestrator/src/services/sub-agent-router.ts:1641-1648` builds a `Memory` with `roomId: target.roomId` and `content.source = ACPX_ROUTER_SOURCE`, which is `MESSAGE_SOURCE_SUB_AGENT` (`:91`).
2. `target.roomId` comes from the origin ladder `originRoomId ?? sourceRoomId ?? taskRoomId ?? roomId` — `services/session-room-binding.ts:45-50` documents the first two as **"the origin connector channel"**, and `services/active-session-forward.ts:50-51` confirms the binding is deliberately connector-agnostic "so plain SMS/WhatsApp follow-ups in the origin channel work too."
3. `sub-agent-router.ts:1768-1772` emits `MESSAGE_RECEIVED` with that memory, so the full pipeline (and therefore the personal-assistant actions) runs on it.
4. `plugins/plugin-personal-assistant/src/actions/scheduled-task.ts:1165` calls `bindScheduledTaskToInboundChat(scope.runtime, message)` on that inbound message in the create path.

At step 4 the message has `content.source === "sub_agent"` and its room is the owner's real connector DM. `inboundSource` is not `"api"` and not `"client_chat"` → falls through `:74`. `room.source` is e.g. `"discord"` and `channelId !== room.id` → falls through `:84`. The binding is captured, and an internally-originated turn has acquired connector dispatch.

### What is *already* covered (so the fix stays narrow)

The third clause, `channelId === room.id`, is load-bearing and does catch a real class: rooms minted by `runtime.ensureConnection` with no channel mapping default `channelId` to `roomId`, which is what the trigger runtime's fallback room does (`packages/agent/src/triggers/runtime.ts:334-339`, `:406-418`). So a *purely synthetic* room is already rejected regardless of its source. **The gap is specifically an internal-provenance turn inside a genuine connector room**, which is precisely the case the `production-wiring` test above says must be rejected.

I have traced this statically and have not run a live end-to-end repro; the fail-open shape against the canonical list is fully determined by the tree either way.

## Proposed Fix

The repo-idiomatic, fail-closed shape already exists ~40 lines away in the same package — `src/lifeops/messaging/owner-send-policy.ts:53-75`:

```ts
/**
 * Exhaustive `MessageSource` membership guard. Core's node entry does not
 * re-export `ALL_MESSAGE_SOURCES`, so membership is pinned locally with a
 * `Record<MessageSource, true>` — the compiler fails this file whenever core
 * adds or removes a source, forcing this boundary to stay in sync.
 */
const MESSAGE_SOURCE_GUARD: Record<MessageSource, true> = { gmail: true, discord: true, /* ... */ };
```

Note that `MessageSource` is the **connector** set, not the internal-sentinel set. That makes the stronger fix an *allowlist* rather than a longer denylist, which also matches this function's own docstring ("Capture the connector destination… Unattested/internal/API turns keep the existing in-app path"):

- Reject the inbound envelope unless its provenance is absent or a known connector — i.e. reject any `MessageSourceSentinel` from core, rather than the two spelled inline.
- Gate the resolved room's `source` through an exhaustive `Record<MessageSource, true>` so only a real connector source can be bound.

Either direction removes the fail-open; the allowlist additionally makes it a **compile error** to add a source to core without revisiting this boundary, which is the property `owner-send-policy.ts` explicitly went out of its way to buy.

Happy to implement this if it is wanted as a contribution — see Claim / Status Notes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A scheduled-task create whose inbound message carries `source: "sub_agent"` returns `null` from `bindScheduledTaskToInboundChat`, even when the resolved room is a valid connector room with `channelId !== room.id`.
- [ ] The same holds for `coding-agent`, `agent_greeting`, and `trigger-prompt`.
- [ ] `client_chat`, `api`, and the `channelId === room.id` synthetic-room case keep returning `null` (no regression on d4b58b496's cases).
- [ ] A genuine connector DM turn (e.g. `source: "discord"`, distinct `channelId`) still produces a binding.
- [ ] Adding a new sentinel to `packages/core/src/types/message-source.ts`, or a new source to `MessageSource`, fails the build or a test at this boundary rather than silently widening it.

5c:T102d,## Summary

The authenticated browser continuation uses the shared onboarding chat endpoint as a provisioning status poll. Every poll omits a user message and an idempotency key, but the backend still generates, appends, and saves an assistant reply. While provisioning is pending, repeated polls therefore grow the durable onboarding transcript with duplicate status copy. When the agent becomes ready, those duplicates are returned to the UI and copied into managed-agent memory.

This affects connector continuations that reach the `PROVISIONING_CHAT` step, including Discord and Telegram once their browser continuation succeeds.

## Deterministic trace on `develop@1232c982c1594d2438a8a53b02e41a9ba86664aa`

1. `ProvisioningChatStep` always activates `useElizaAppProvisioningChat(true, onboardingSessionId)`.
2. The shared-onboarding branch POSTs once on mount, then the polling effect POSTs immediately and every 5 seconds. Those requests contain only `sessionId` and `platform`; they contain no `message` and no `idempotencyKey`:
   - [initial request](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/1232c982c1594d2438a8a53b02e41a9ba86664aa/packages/homepage/src/lib/hooks/use-eliza-app-provisioning-chat.ts#L122-L153)
   - [immediate and interval polling](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/1232c982c1594d2438a8a53b02e41a9ba86664aa/packages/homepage/src/lib/hooks/use-eliza-app-provisioning-chat.ts#L165-L243)
3. Each backend invocation unconditionally derives a reply, appends it as an assistant message, and saves the session:
   - [unconditional append/save](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/1232c982c1594d2438a8a53b02e41a9ba86664aa/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/eliza-app/onboarding-chat.ts#L821-L849)
4. The handoff serializes the complete history and sends it to `/api/memory/remember`; this happens when the status first becomes running, before the current poll reply is appended:
   - [whole-history serialization and remember call](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/1232c982c1594d2438a8a53b02e41a9ba86664aa/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/eliza-app/onboarding-chat.ts#L591-L636)
   - [running-state handoff](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/1232c982c1594d2438a8a53b02e41a9ba86664aa/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/eliza-app/onboarding-chat.ts#L812-L819)
5. The existing unit contract explicitly proves that a second empty/whitespace turn adds a second assistant-only history entry:
   - [empty-turn regression contract](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/blob/1232c982c1594d2438a8a53b02e41a9ba86664aa/packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/eliza-app/onboarding-chat.test.ts#L685-L700)

Provisioning status checks must be read-only with respect to chat history. The proactive empty first turn may create one welcome, but subsequent status polls for an existing session must not append assistant messages or alter the handoff transcript.

- The initial proactive welcome remains available exactly once.

5e:T4b5,## Problem\n\nPR #17873 merged with two outstanding egress findings:\n\n1. `sendReplyWithRetry` replays `message.reply()` without a Discord nonce. An ambiguous 5xx/socket failure after Discord accepted the first request can create duplicate replies, compounded by discord.js REST retries.\n2. Exhausted route or reply attempts only log and return, leaving the user with the same silent dropped-turn outcome the retry work is intended to remove.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- One logical inbound Discord message cannot create duplicate outbound replies during ambiguous transport failures. Prefer the transport library’s existing retry behavior unless a stable Discord-supported dedupe key is proven end to end.\n- Exhausted managed-route and reply-send failures produce a short, visibly distinct fallback response when delivery remains possible.\n- The fallback path is bounded and cannot recurse into the same retry helper.\n- Deterministic 4xx behavior remains fail-fast.\n- Unit tests cover ambiguous/transient failure ownership, route exhaustion, send exhaustion, and fallback failure logging.\n- Gateway Discord tests, typecheck, lint, and the required repository gates pass.\n\nRelates to #17873.5f:Ta57,## Symptom

Once an eliza-app onboarding provision ends in `error`, the messaging surface is permanently wedged for that organization. Every subsequent message replies:

> I hit a provisioning issue, `<name>`. Your control panel has the latest status, and the team can inspect it there.

forever. No retry is ever attempted, no matter how many messages are sent or how much time passes. Reproduced live: a user whose provision hard-failed during the #17880 outage cannot get a working agent by messaging again.

## Cause

`ensureElizaAppProvisioning` early-returns on the presence of **any** sandbox row, without looking at its status:

```ts
const existing = await getElizaAppProvisioningStatus(params.organizationId);
if (existing.sandbox) {
  return existing;          // <- an `error` row returns here too
}
```

`getElizaAppProvisioningStatus` takes `sandboxes[0]` from `listByOrganization`, which orders `created_at DESC` — so the newest row wins, and a fresh failure permanently shadows any older healthy row.

The early return is correct for `pending` / `provisioning` / `running` (that is the idempotency guard that stops duplicate provisioning). It is wrong for terminal states.

## Expected

A terminal sandbox state should not block a new provision from the onboarding path. Concretely, the guard should early-return only for non-terminal rows and fall through to `createAgent` + `enqueueAgentProvision` otherwise (`createAgent` already takes `reuseExistingNonTerminal: true`, so the notion of "non-terminal" already exists one layer down and should be the same predicate here).

Points needing a decision in the fix:

- **Which states are terminal for this purpose** — `error` certainly; `deletion_failed` / `stopped` need a deliberate call rather than an implicit one.
- **Retry throttling.** A node that is genuinely broken would otherwise be retried on every inbound message. A minimum interval since the last failed attempt, or reusing the placement circuit breaker from #17880, keeps a hard-down fleet from being hammered per-message.
- **What the user is told meanwhile.** The current copy points at a control panel; if onboarding now self-heals, the message should say a retry is under way rather than sending the user elsewhere.

## Workaround until fixed

Delete the errored agent from the control panel; the next message provisions a fresh one.

## Context

- #17880 — the outage that produced the errored rows (and the placement circuit breaker that reduces how often they are created).
- 8 `agent_provision` jobs hard-failed in that window; every one of those organizations is in this state right now.

63:Te01,## Symptom

Thirteen production agents cannot be deleted. Every one carries the same error, and the set is still growing — the oldest has been stuck since **29 July**, the newest joined **2 August**:

```
13 rows  |  2026-07-29 → 2026-08-02  |  status: deletion_failed / deletion_pending
Deletion permanently failed after 3 attempts: value.toISOString is not a function
```

Each of these agents burned its full three-attempt budget, flipped to a terminal state, and now sits there. From the customer's side the agent will not go away.

## Cause

Raw Drizzle rows carry `timestamptz` as **strings**, not `Date` objects — the identity type parsers installed in `node-postgres/session.cjs` see to that, while typed select builders return a ms-truncated `Date` via `mapFromDriverValue`. The deletion retry path read a raw row and called `.toISOString()` on a value that was a string, so every retry threw before it could do any work. Three attempts, three identical crashes, terminal failure.

## The fix already exists and is already in `main`

`e923a5cbb66` — *fix(cloud): unbreak deletion retries crashing on raw-row string timestamps (#17260)* — merged to `develop`, then to `main` via the promote in #17300 on 30 July. It was validated end to end on staging: a seeded `deletion_failed` row went to `ROW DELETED` on the next sweep.

**It has never reached production.** The production control plane still runs `054fc9feff` — a 24 July merge, nine days old:

```
$ ssh <prod-cp> 'cd /opt/eliza && git log -1'
054fc9feff   (9 days ago)
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor e923a5cbb66 HEAD  →  false
```

## Why it never shipped

`deploy-eliza-provisioning-worker.yml` is what puts this code on the control plane, and it deploys production only from `main`. **The repository's PR template and the contribution skill are mutually incompatible: following both — as both documents instruct — always produces an invalid attribution marker.** The published ledger shows the result: of 67 eligible sources, **3 are valid and 64 are missing or invalid (95.5% failure)**, including PRs authored by @lalalune (#17424, #17555).

This costs **zero points** — `leaderboard.ts:1379` states plainly that complete, partial, missing, and invalid attribution states *"add no points."* I am not filing this for score. It breaks the **provenance dataset itself**, which is the stated purpose of the whole attribution system: the public `attributions`, `attributionCoverage`, and `invalidAttributionMarkers` fields currently describe almost nothing that actually happened.

I am implementing this (file-and-fix); PR follows in this session.

## Root cause

`markerFooterError` (`packages/eliza-computer/src/lib/leaderboard.ts:1035-1046`) requires **exactly one** of each visible row across the *entire body*:

```ts
const providerModelLines = attributionLineValues(body, "AI provider/model");
const clientLines        = attributionLineValues(body, "Client / agent tooling");
const skillRevisionLines = attributionLineValues(body, "(?:Contribution skill revision|Skill revision)");
const statusLines        = attributionLineValues(body, "Attribution status");
if (providerModelLines.length !== 1 || clientLines.length !== 1 ||
    skillRevisionLines.length !== 1 || statusLines.length !== 1) {
  return "marker requires exactly one complete visible attribution footer";
}
```

But `.github/pull_request_template.md:28-37` already ships three of those exact labels as checklist rows:

```markdown
<!-- attribution-row:client -->
- Client / agent tooling: `client-name` / `None - human-only contribution`
<!-- attribution-row:skill-revision -->
- Skill revision: `owner/repo@full-commit-sha:path` / `N/A - no contribution skill used`
<!-- attribution-row:status -->
- Attribution status: `self-reported`
```

…and `SKILL.md` instructs: *"In a PR body, complete every stable contribution-attribution row in the repository template **and append this footer after the template**"* — where the footer repeats `Client / agent tooling`, `Contribution skill revision`, and `Attribution status`. Note the skill-revision regex accepts **both** spellings, so the template's `Skill revision` row and the footer's `Contribution skill revision` row both count.

Every label therefore appears twice, `length !== 1` fires, and the marker is rejected. The contributor did everything both documents asked.

## Executable repro

Real validator, real template, no mocks — three cases, isolating the cause to a single line:

```ts
import { assessModelAttribution } from "packages/eliza-computer/src/lib/leaderboard.ts";
// FOOT(extra) = `extra` + the exact 5-line footer from SKILL.md + the v1 marker
run(FOOT(""),                                          "A. footer alone");
run(FOOT("- Attribution status: `self-reported`\n\n"), "B. ONE template row above the footer");
run(FOOT(templateClientSkillStatusRows),               "C. the real template's 3 rows above the footer");
```

```
A. footer alone (no template rows):
   valid=1 invalid=0
B. ONE template attribution row above the footer:
   valid=1 invalid=1 marker requires exactly one complete visible attribution footer
C. the real template's 3 rows above the footer:
   valid=1 invalid=1 marker requires exactly one complete visible attribution footer
```

And end-to-end with the shipped template plus the skill's prescribed footer — the exact body a compliant contributor produces:

```
1. .github/pull_request_template.md + footer appended after it (as SKILL.md instructs):
   valid=1 invalid=1 marker requires exactly one complete visible attribution footer
```

The `visible-declaration` is parsed fine in every case; it is the **marker** that is rejected, which is why the ledger shows a valid declaration alongside an invalid marker for the same source.

## Second, independent defect: `scripts/pr-evidence.mjs` breaks marker finality

`markerFooterError:1031` also requires `body.slice(markerRecord.end).trim()` to be empty — the marker must be the final content. But `patchRow` (`scripts/pr-evidence.mjs:332-339`) appends when a row marker is absent:

```js
if (at === -1) {
  // Row marker absent (old template) — append a fresh marker + row.
  return `${body.trimEnd()}\n\n${marker}\n${line}\n`;
}
```

`patchEvidenceHead:353-364` appends the same way when there is no `# Evidence Gate` heading. So the official evidence tool, run against a body whose footer is last (exactly where SKILL.md puts it), relocates content **after** the marker and invalidates it — the `"marker must be the final source content"` reason. I hit this on four of my own PRs before catching it; the fix on my side was manual re-ordering, which no instruction tells a contributor to do.

## Proposed fix

1. **Scope the footer scan to the terminal declaration block** rather than the whole body. The rule's intent is "exactly one *footer*", not "exactly one occurrence of each label anywhere in the document" — a checklist row 90 lines above the footer is not a competing footer. Concretely: collect the contiguous run of declaration lines ending at the validated terminal lane signature, and count labels only within it. This keeps every genuinely-duplicated footer rejected, keeps footer-only bodies valid (no regression for the current 3), and makes template + footer valid — which is what both documents already tell contributors to produce.
2. **Make `pr-evidence.mjs` footer-aware**: when appending a fresh row marker or head marker, insert **before** a trailing attribution footer instead of after it, so the official tools compose.
3. Tests for both: template+footer valid; two complete footers still invalid; footer-only still valid; `patchRow`/`patchEvidenceHead` preserve marker finality.

Alternative considered and rejected as worse: renaming the template rows to avoid collision. It would fix new PRs while leaving the skill's "append after the template" instruction producing near-miss bodies, and it churns a file every contributor sees.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A body built from `.github/pull_request_template.md` + the SKILL.md footer validates with `valid=1 invalid=0` (executable test, real template).
- [ ] Two complete attribution footers in one body still fail with the existing reason (no weakening).
- [ ] A footer-only body still validates (no regression against the currently-valid sources).
- [ ] `patchRow` and `patchEvidenceHead` leave the attribution marker as the final content when one is present; covered red/green.
- [ ] `bun test packages/eliza-computer` and the `scripts/pr-evidence` tests pass.

68:T136a,## Summary

When `composeState` coalesces a provider execution (`providerExecutionsInFlight`, keyed `message.id + provider + audience`), every later caller awaits a promise wired to the **first** caller's cancellation signal and deadline. The waiter cannot cancel the work it is awaiting, and the first caller's abort propagates into turns that never requested it.

I am implementing this (file-and-fix); the PR will be coordinated with #17508's landing since that PR rewrites the same hunks (see coordination note below).

## Reproduced on `develop` (`9bdcf068b`) — and it survives on the #17508 head

`packages/core/src/runtime.ts` (develop):

- `:4590` — `providerSignal` is resolved once per `composeState` call (`turnControllers.signalFor(message.roomId) ?? getStreamingContext()?.abortSignal`).
- `:4617-4626` — the promise is built with **that** signal and **that** caller's budget: `withProviderDeadline((signal) => …, providerBudgetMs, provider.name, providerSignal)`.
- `:4605` / `:4645` — a later caller that hits the map does a raw `const result = await execution.promise;` — no race against the *waiting* caller's own signal, no reference counting.

Consequences (both directions):

- **Waiter B aborts →** nothing is cancelled. B's turn continues consuming A's execution until A's deadline/settlement, so B's "stop" does not stop provider work.
- **Owner A aborts (or times out) →** B's await rejects with A's `TurnAbortedError`/timeout, and B's turn dies with a cancellation its user never issued. The current-signal outcome classification at `:4667` labels it with B's `providerSignal` state, so the trajectory can even *misattribute* whose abort it was.

On the #17508 head (`ebea48b`), the deadline is replaced by owner cancellation but the coalescing shape is identical (`withProviderCancellation(…, providerSignal)` captured once; waiters await verbatim) — I re-derived both directions there in https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/pull/17508#issuecomment-5150514957, and @lalalune independently reproduced the same two items on the prior head (2026-08-01T08:49Z review comment on #17508). So this defect is a property of the coalescing pattern, not of either deadline/cancellation architecture.

## Repair proposal

Keep one shared underlying execution, give each waiter its own boundary:

1. At the await site, race `execution.promise` against the **current** caller's `providerSignal` so a waiter's abort detaches that waiter immediately (rejecting with *its* reason, not the owner's).
2. Reference-count the underlying execution; abort the shared work only when every attached waiter has aborted/detached — a shared execution with one live waiter keeps running.
3. Classify each caller's outcome against its own signal (the `:4667` classification already reads the current signal; it just never gets the chance today because the shared rejection arrives first).

Works identically on the deadline architecture (develop) and the owner-cancellation architecture (#17508).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A coalesced waiter whose own signal aborts stops awaiting immediately and rejects with its own reason; the shared execution keeps running for the remaining owner.
- [ ] The first caller's abort no longer rejects other waiters with the first caller's reason; each waiter resolves normally if the underlying work settles, or rejects with its own abort.
- [ ] The shared execution is aborted exactly when the last attached caller aborts (reference counting), covered by a deterministic unit test with two concurrent `composeState` calls on the same `message.id + provider`.
- [ ] Existing coalescing behavior (single execution per key, cleanup on settle) unchanged; `bun run --cwd packages/core test` green.

## Evidence plan

- Real-LLM trajectories: N/A — deterministic runtime concurrency behavior; deterministic unit tests drive the real `composeState` path.
- Logs: failing test on current develop (both directions), passing after; full test-lane run.
- Screenshots/video: N/A — no UI.
- Domain artifact: the failing-then-passing test transcript.

## Coordination note

#17508 rewrites these hunks. To avoid churning a core PR: if #17508 lands first, my fix targets its `withProviderCancellation` shape; if this lands first, it is a small, rebASE-friendly change to the await site + map entry. Either way the failing tests are architecture-agnostic (they assert waiter-boundary semantics, not implementation).

6b:Ta0a,## Problem

`eliza-core-prod-1` (88.99.66.168) is simultaneously:

- a **production agent placement node** (16 declared slots, agent containers with live users), and
- the **self-hosted GitHub Actions farm** for `elizaOS/eliza` — 22 `actions-runner@N` systemd services under `/opt/actions-runners/`, running up to ~11 concurrent CI jobs.

These two workloads compete for the same SATA RAID-1. CI jobs are IO-heavy (bun installs, turbo builds, cache tar extraction, docker-in-CI container churn), and on 2026-08-06 ~11:41 UTC their combined load saturated the disks: IO pressure `full` ~78% sustained, load average 451, 366 D-state processes, `systemd-journald` dying on its watchdog. Result: `docker create` on the node could no longer complete inside the provisioner's 60s timeout, and since every OTHER node is over its declared capacity (#17866), the placement selector had nowhere else to go — **fleet-wide provisioning outage for every new agent** (#17880).

This is a structural conflict, not a one-off: CI load is bursty and unbounded (a busy PR day = a saturated node), while agent provisioning needs predictable IO latency on the same box. Any future CI spike reproduces the outage.

## What "separated" should mean

One of, in order of preference:

1. **Move the runner farm off agent-placement nodes entirely** — dedicated CI box(es), or Hetzner Cloud autoscaled runners. Agent nodes run agents, full stop.
2. If co-location must stay for cost reasons: **fence CI IO and CPU** with systemd cgroup limits on the runner slices (`IOWeight`, `io.max`, `CPUQuota`, `TasksMax`) so CI can never starve dockerd/agent workloads, and **cap runner concurrency** to what the disks actually sustain.
3. At minimum: **remove `eliza-core-prod-1` from the placement pool** (capacity 0 / disabled) and accept it as a CI-only box — requires fleet capacity to land first (#17866), otherwise there is no placement target left.

Whichever option is chosen, the placement-side hardening (per-node circuit breaker + IO-pressure-aware readiness probe, tracked in #17880) is complementary, not a substitute: the scheduler should survive a sick node, AND prod nodes shouldn't be made sick by CI.

## Context

- #17880 — the outage this caused (2026-08-06/07), with full node-level measurements.
- #17866 — fleet over declared capacity; why this node was the only placement candidate.
- Ops note: the 8 `agent_provision` jobs that hard-failed during the outage and the 2 agents stuck in replacement-cleanup loops (`d6e37e91`, `f27f096d`) are listed in #17880.

6c:Ta81,## Problem

`MainActivity.onCreate()` unconditionally calls
`ElizaWorkScheduler.enqueuePeriodic()`. On a real LP3 using the
paired-LAN/remote runtime, Capacitor Preferences has no
`eliza:device-secret`, so `ElizaTasksWorker` wakes every 15 minutes and returns
`Result.failure()` before it can deliver `/api/internal/wake`.

Physical-device log evidence on 2026-08-06:

```text
15:15:19.624 WM-WorkerWrapper: Starting work for ai.elizaos.app.ElizaTasksWorker
15:15:19.625 ElizaTasksWorker: device secret not provisioned; skipping wake (permanent failure until JS writes it)
15:15:19.628 WM-WorkerWrapper: Worker result FAILURE
15:30:19.654 WM-WorkerWrapper: Starting work for ai.elizaos.app.ElizaTasksWorker
15:30:19.654 ElizaTasksWorker: device secret not provisioned; skipping wake (permanent failure until JS writes it)
15:30:19.658 WM-WorkerWrapper: Worker result FAILURE
```

This did **not** crash or restart the app; Android `ApplicationExitInfo` shows
only development APK replacements and explicit force-stops today. It is still
unnecessary work, noisy diagnostics, and a broken ownership contract.

The boot receiver already checks `eliza:background-enabled`, but
`MainActivity` does not. Neither `eliza:device-secret` nor
`eliza:agent-base` is part of the current native storage sync set, so the
schedule can be present with no deliverable target.

## Correct boundary

Periodic wake work should be reconciled from the selected runtime and
background preference, not blindly enqueued. A remote paired runtime with no
native wake credentials must have no scheduled phone-local wake. A committed
local/hybrid runtime should schedule only after the wake credential/target is
actually provisioned. Disabling background work or changing away from an owned
target should cancel the unique work.

Do not convert the worker's missing-credential failure into fake success and do
not add an aggressive retry/watchdog.

## Acceptance criteria

- MainActivity and boot/package-replace paths use one idempotent schedule/cancel authority.
- The authority requires background enabled plus a valid wake target/credential owned by the selected runtime.
- Remote paired mode with no credentials leaves no `ElizaTasksWorker` JobScheduler entry and emits no 15-minute failure.
- Local/hybrid mode with valid credentials still delivers a real authenticated `/api/internal/wake`.
- Switching modes or disabling background cancels stale unique work; provisioning a valid target schedules it.
- Focused unit/source-generation tests cover schedule, cancel, missing-secret, local, hybrid, and remote cases.
- Real Android evidence includes `dumpsys jobscheduler`, worker logs, and no app process restart.
6d:T25ad,## Summary

Productionize the BlueBubbles → Eliza Cloud phone gateway on a dedicated Mac and make self-message loops impossible by construction.

A live same-Apple-Account test exposed two coupled failures:

1. A Mac signed into personal and gateway Messages identities allowed unrelated personal traffic to reach the relay.
2. Sending from the gateway number to itself produced alternating BlueBubbles copies (`isFromMe: true` and `isFromMe: false`) whose sender and receiving identity were both the gateway. The relay treated the false copy as new inbound traffic, sent the agent reply back to the gateway, and repeated until the relay was stopped.

The launchd process also received `SQLITE_AUTH` when trying to read `~/Library/Messages/chat.db`. Safety decisions must not depend on direct Messages DB access or Full Disk Access.

This issue covers the dedicated-Mac deployment runbook, an idempotent installer, sender/account linking, private-API readiness, loop prevention, and real end-to-end proof.

## Security model

This deployment intentionally disables SIP for the BlueBubbles private API. It must run on a dedicated gateway Mac only:

- No personal Apple Account, phone number, email identity, Messages history, or daily-driver data.
- Use a dedicated macOS user and dedicated Apple Account for the gateway number.
- Enable FileVault, automatic security updates, and the host firewall.
- Bind BlueBubbles to localhost/LAN as narrowly as practical; do not expose its password or local API directly to the public Internet.
- Store relay secrets in a mode-`0600` file and never print them in logs, screenshots, issues, or CI.
- Keep BlueBubbles and the relay local-only; Cloud remains the authenticated public boundary.
- Disabling SIP is a human-owned recovery-mode step and must be documented with the associated security tradeoff.

## Required behavior

### Identity isolation

- Subscribe only to BlueBubbles `new-message` events.
- Before contacting Cloud, retrieve the full message through the authenticated local BlueBubbles API and verify `chats[].lastAddressedHandle === BLUEBUBBLES_GATEWAY_PHONE_NUMBER`.
- Fail closed when the receiving identity is absent, cannot be retrieved, or differs from the configured gateway.
- Reject every `isFromMe: true` event.
- Reject every inbound event whose sender/peer normalizes to the gateway number (`gateway_self_message`).
- Refuse every outbound send whose derived recipient normalizes to the gateway number.
- Do not use a configured fallback identity to reinterpret an uncertain `isFromMe` event.
- Never depend on `chat.db` access for a safety decision.

The relevant implementation is `packages/cloud/scripts/bluebubbles-local-bridge.ts`; regression coverage belongs in `packages/cloud/scripts/bluebubbles-local-bridge.registered-e2e.test.ts`.

### User/agent routing

The gateway is sender-owned:

- An E.164 sender identity resolves to that sender's signed-in Eliza Cloud user.
- The signed-in connectors flow must verify/link the phone identity to the intended Cloud account.
- Exactly one non-gateway running sandbox should be selected for that owner.
- An unknown sender receives the secure sign-in/onboarding continuation.
- A known user without an agent receives provisioning/onboarding state, never a fabricated agent response.
- A stopped agent, insufficient credits, ambiguous agents, and login/link failures are explicit states.
- Once the user signs in, the next message must route to their agent without retaining a stale negative lookup.

The UI must make the current phone-to-account-to-agent binding visible and revocable.

## Dedicated Mac setup

### 1. Base system

- Install the repository-pinned Bun and Node versions.
- Clone this repository and run:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza.git
cd eliza
bun run install:light
```

- Install BlueBubbles Server from its official release.
- In Messages → Settings → iMessage:
  - enable only the dedicated gateway number under “You can be reached for messages at”;
  - select the gateway number under “Start new conversations from”;
  - disable every personal number and email identity.
- From macOS Recovery, disable SIP as the human owner, reboot, then follow the official BlueBubbles private-API/helper setup.
- Verify locally:
  - `csrutil status` reports disabled;
  - BlueBubbles reports private API enabled;
  - the private API helper is connected;
  - an outbound BlueBubbles private-API send works before installing the relay.

### 2. Register the gateway in Cloud

From an authenticated Eliza Cloud account:

```http
POST /api/v1/phone-gateways/bluebubbles
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <ELIZA_CLOUD_ACCESS_TOKEN>

{
  "routingMode": "sender-owned",
  "phoneNumber": "+1XXXXXXXXXX",
  "friendlyName": "Dedicated iPhone gateway"
}
```

Save the one-time `relayEnvironment` response locally. Cloud must store only the token digest.

### 3. Relay environment

Create `.eliza-local/bluebubbles-bridge.env` with mode `0600`:

```sh
ELIZA_CLOUD_BLUEBUBBLES_URL=https://api.elizacloud.ai/api/webhooks/bluebubbles/<BRIDGE_ID>
BLUEBUBBLES_BRIDGE_ID=<BRIDGE_ID>
BLUEBUBBLES_GATEWAY_TOKEN=<ONE_TIME_TOKEN>
BLUEBUBBLES_GATEWAY_PHONE_NUMBER=+1XXXXXXXXXX
BLUEBUBBLES_SEND_METHOD=private-api
BLUEBUBBLES_LOOPBACK_NORMALIZATION_ENABLED=false
BLUEBUBBLES_PENDING_RETRY_ENABLED=false
```

Do not duplicate the BlueBubbles password when the relay can read it from BlueBubbles' local config DB. If an explicit password is required, keep it in this mode-`0600` file and redact it everywhere else.

### 4. LaunchAgent

Add a repository-owned installer that renders `~/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.elizacloud.bluebubbles-bridge.plist` using absolute paths. The generated service should run:

```sh
/bin/zsh -c 'set -a; source <repo>/.eliza-local/bluebubbles-bridge.env; set +a; exec <bun> run packages/cloud/scripts/bluebubbles-local-bridge.ts'
```

with:

- `WorkingDirectory=<repo>`
- `RunAtLoad=true`
- `KeepAlive=true`
- stdout/stderr under `<repo>/.eliza-local/`
- no secrets embedded in the plist.

Installer lifecycle:

```sh
launchctl bootout "gui/$(id -u)" "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.elizacloud.bluebubbles-bridge.plist" 2>/dev/null || true
launchctl bootstrap "gui/$(id -u)" "$HOME/Library/LaunchAgents/ai.elizacloud.bluebubbles-bridge.plist"
launchctl kickstart -k "gui/$(id -u)/ai.elizacloud.bluebubbles-bridge"
```

The installer must be idempotent, validate file permissions, and support `install`, `uninstall`, `status`, and `doctor`.

### 5. Readiness

```sh
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8795/health
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8795/diagnostics
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8795/doctor
curl -fsS http://127.0.0.1:8795/inbound-events
```

Ready means:

- registered-device Cloud auth;
- expected gateway number;
- BlueBubbles reachable;
- exactly one relay webhook for `new-message`;
- `private-api` outbound readiness true;
- helper connected and SIP disabled;
- zero pending replies;
- no TCC/SQLite dependency in the ingress safety path.

## End-to-end verification

Use an external phone that is not signed into the gateway Apple Account.

### Negative gates

1. Message addressed to a different local identity:
   - response: `gateway_target_mismatch`;
   - zero Cloud requests;
   - zero outbound sends.
2. Message whose target identity cannot be proved:
   - response: `gateway_target_unverified`;
   - zero Cloud requests;
   - zero outbound sends.
3. Message from the gateway to itself, covering both BlueBubbles copies:
   - `isFromMe: true` → `outbound_message`;
   - `isFromMe: false`, sender equals gateway → `gateway_self_message`;
   - outbound validation to the gateway fails;
   - no reply is queued;
   - message count remains stable for at least five minutes.
4. Replay the same GUID:
   - one Cloud dispatch maximum;
   - one outbound reply maximum.

### Positive physical proof

```sh
bun run --cwd packages/app-core sms-gateway:verify:bluebubbles-registered -- \
  --sender +1EXTERNAL_NUMBER \
  --agent-id <EXPECTED_AGENT_ID> \
  --wait-real \
  --timeout-seconds 180
```

Acceptance evidence must show:

- the physical message reached BlueBubbles and was addressed to the gateway identity;
- Cloud resolved the sender to the expected signed-in user, organization, and agent;
- the real running agent produced the reply;
- BlueBubbles private API sent it to the external sender;
- the receiving phone displays the dedicated gateway number as sender;
- relay `/inbound-events` records `handled: true`, the expected agent ID, `replied: true`, and `replyQueued: false`;
- no unrelated personal conversation was read or answered;
- the path still works after reboot.

6e:T137b,Production release: promotes `develop` → `main`, which deploys the Worker to `api.elizacloud.ai` and the Pages projects to the apex + `app.elizacloud.ai`.

## Why now

Headline fix: **half of all production inference requests fail** with "Billing authorization is warming up" — a strict success/failure alternation reproduced live (8-call probe: 4 ok / 4 warming; raw inference 0.49–1.48s throughout, so the model path is healthy and the auth gate is the defect). The fix (#17745, republish the org-balance gate hint after a debit) has been on `develop` since before this cycle; production is the only place it has not landed.

Also shipping, user-facing:
- **App-mode onboarding** (#17752): logging in on `app.elizacloud.ai` lands in *your* dedicated agent — automatic entry, chooser, resume, error fallback. Evidence: live before/after captures, walkthrough video, OCR review on the PR.
- **Cross-origin SSO** (#17788): one login across the dashboard and app origins — atomic single-use codes on Postgres, fail-closed logout, PKCE binding; hardened after security review.
- **Fired reminders deliver their content** (#17776), never a bare acknowledgement.
- **Node embedding sidecar** (#17787): provisioning installs it, health-checks probe it, self-heal converges the fleet — closing the "sidecars wiped again" regression loop.
- Latency hot-path work (#17743 lineage) and the rest of 448 commits of fixes.

Also shipping, operational: the certification pipeline itself was restored and made runnable (#17790, #17792, #17794, #17796–#17799, #17802 — the workflows had been deleted by an accidental sweep, and the chain had never run end to end; it now produces the signed certification this PR carries, and caught a real unlisted-public-route gap in review).

| `0185_job_execution_interruptions` | `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` (integer, default 0) |

| `0187_agent_sandbox_lifecycle_revision` | guarded column + `CREATE OR REPLACE` function + trigger replace (`DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS` → recreate — idempotent pattern) |
| `0188_sso_bridge_store` | 2 new tables + index, all `IF NOT EXISTS` |

No destructive ops, no data rewrites, no `DELETE`/`TRUNCATE`/table drops anywhere in the set.

## Summary

Hardens the existing Google Calendar push callback path as one security boundary:

- registers no public callback route unless validated runtime webhook settings explicitly enable it
- verifies a destination-bound `gcalwh.v1` HMAC capability before service resolution or DB access
- authorizes account, grant, and audience before any notification, lease, receipt, limiter, or provisional resource-binding write
- applies independent durable principal and destination limits after authentication and authorization
- supports a bounded current/previous key ring plus explicit emergency revocation
- writes a typed immutable ingress receipt transactionally with exactly-once enqueue semantics
- preserves header/body bounds, replay suppression, conditional SQL advancement, leases, retries, and provider refetch

## Security proof

Focused tests traverse the real plugin route/runtime and PGlite production schema:

- default config has no route
- disabled, malformed, bad-signature, stale, wrong-resource, replayed, and mismatched-account callbacks execute no provider sync and create no receipt/pending state
- stateless rejects do not resolve `CalendarService`
- rate-limited authenticated callbacks return `429` before receipt/enqueue/sync
- previous-key callbacks work during rotation and fail after explicit revocation while the key remains configured
- one valid callback processes once and persists one bounded receipt with key/account/grant/calendar provenance

- `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-calendar format:check`
- `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-calendar lint:check`
- `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-calendar typecheck`
- `bun run --cwd plugins/plugin-calendar build`
- `bun test test/google-calendar-watch.pglite.test.ts src/routes/plugin-routes.test.ts test/calendar-plugin-routes.test.ts` from `plugins/plugin-calendar`, 23 passed
- `git diff --check origin/develop...HEAD`

# Integration rationale

This is intentionally one closeout because the affected seams share a single executable contract. Runtime/config and voice selection establish the authenticated capability contract; Cloud admission and pricing enforce it; pendant/conversation ownership consumes the same authenticated runtime and canonical persistence boundaries; and the app surfaces are the end-to-end consumer. Splitting those pieces would create intermediate revisions with only one side of a producer/consumer contract and would require duplicate or temporarily weaker evidence.

The CI and harness corrections are part of certifying that integrated state: they were exposed by the full matrix and make the exact candidate reproducible under clean-install, isolated, browser, native-audit, and fixture lanes. Keeping the set together provides one tested integration and rollback point for the gaps found while validating already-merged #17733.

# Risks

Low and interaction-only. This changes pager release settlement so a fast intentional flick chooses the adjacent page instead of bouncing back. Direction is limited to the adjacent page, vertical gestures remain rejected, and click suppression is covered in a real Chromium interaction.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

It gives fast horizontal flicks a velocity-aware release projection while keeping slow drags distance-based. Release direction is derived from the actual gesture, clamped to one adjacent page, and settled through the existing pager animation path. A style-resolution barrier preserves the final dragged frame before the controlled page target is applied, preventing Chromium from coalescing release and settle into a visible snap.

## What kind of change is this?

UI interaction bug fix.

76:T1aeb,`hardenIncomingUserMessage` wraps external `content.text` in the untrusted-content security envelope in place. Every action that fell back to `message.content.text` as a query, name, or target was therefore holding the full envelope (markers + provenance header + payload), and several echoed it verbatim to the user — a live leak of the security armor into chat (tj-2dc95f75456876).

Fixes, applied repo-wide (~60 files):

- `unwrapUserMessageText` — a shared read-side seam in core that returns the payload for envelope-wrapped messages and trimmed raw text otherwise; exported from every core entrypoint
- shape-gated display helpers (`describeUserReference` / `userReferenceLogView` and per-plugin equivalents) so blob-shaped references are described, never echoed
- every `message.content.text` fallback across the action surface unwrapped; every user-visible echo clamped
- task `originalRequest` stores the unwrapped payload, not the armor
- honest routing copy for app-create/deploy asks, replacing text that implied the wrong lane
- `outbound-envelope-tripwire`: if the envelope ever reaches an outbound message again through any future path, MESSAGE_SENT reports it via `runtime.reportError` with a clamped preview — detection only, never a silent rewrite

Regression tests added at every fixed site (envelope-echo suites across app-control, cloud-apps, agent-skills, music, calendar, linear, personal-assistant, agent-orchestrator, and core), plus incoming-message-security coverage of the seam itself. All touched-package suites green; typecheck clean across the nine touched packages. Core security/feature suites re-run after the lint fixup: 119 files, 904 tests green.

77:T10cc,# Relates to

Fixes a silent bug where standalone elizaOS agents (no LifeOps) would never reply on Discord, Telegram, iMessage, Signal, WhatsApp, or Matrix because `lifeOpsPassiveConnectorsEnabled()` defaulted to `true` even when `plugin-personal-assistant` was not loaded.

- [x] This PR targets `develop` and is rebased onto the latest `origin/develop` with zero conflicts.
- [x] `bun test packages/core/src/__tests__/lifeops-passive-connectors.test.ts` passes (15/15, 100% coverage).
- [x] A reviewer can confirm the change works without reading the code, from the evidence attached below.

# Sync with develop

- [x] Rebased/merged onto the latest `origin/develop`; zero conflicts.
- [x] `bun run verify` — lint and typecheck pass on changed files; two pre-existing Biome errors in unrelated payment/messaging test files are not introduced by this PR.

# Risks

Low. The change only affects the **default** fallback path — agents that already set `ELIZA_LIFEOPS_PASSIVE_CONNECTORS=false` (or `=true`) are unaffected because explicit settings continue to win. LifeOps agents that load `plugin-personal-assistant` continue to get passive mode automatically. Standalone agents that don't load that plugin now correctly default to active-reply mode.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

`lifeOpsPassiveConnectorsEnabled()` in `packages/core/src/lifeops-passive-connectors.ts` used to return `true` by default when no env var was set. Every connector (Discord, Telegram, iMessage, Signal, WhatsApp, Matrix) gates auto-reply on this function, so any agent without `ELIZA_LIFEOPS_PASSIVE_CONNECTORS=false` in its `.env` would silently ingest messages into memory and never generate a reply.

The fix adds plugin-presence detection as the new fallback:

**Priority order (unchanged for explicit settings):**
1. Runtime setting via `getSetting(...)` — always wins
2. `ELIZA_LIFEOPS_PASSIVE_CONNECTORS` / `LIFEOPS_PASSIVE_CONNECTORS` env var — wins over detection
3. **New:** whether `@elizaos/plugin-personal-assistant` is in `runtime.plugins` — passive on if loaded, passive off otherwise

`SettingsReader` gains an optional `plugins?: Array<{ name: string }>` field — structurally compatible with `IAgentRuntime.plugins: Plugin[]` and all existing connector call sites that pass `this.runtime`.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix — behaviour change only in the default (no env var) path for agents not loading the LifeOps plugin.

# Documentation changes needed?

No. The env var `ELIZA_LIFEOPS_PASSIVE_CONNECTORS=false` workaround documented in some deployment guides still works and can be removed at operators' convenience, but is not required.

# Testing

## Where should a reviewer start?

`packages/core/src/lifeops-passive-connectors.ts` — the diff is 25 lines. Then `packages/core/src/__tests__/lifeops-passive-connectors.test.ts` for the new unit tests.

#17863 landed as `738d605ebc8aea093ab5fd38a40b12761f3b84a5`, providing the provider-independent private `VOICE_DM` response contract.

# What changed

- Replaces the Deepgram Flux realtime STT adapter with Cartesia Ink 2 while keeping Cartesia Sonic 3.5 for streamed TTS.
- Adds the local voice gateway used by the web preview to run Ink -> local elizaOS runtime/Cerebras -> Sonic without Eliza Cloud auth.
- Moves realtime ownership onto the always-mounted home `ChatOverlay` Talk control.
- Persists voice turns in canonical chat history, clears the composer after send, and keeps reconnect/resync state coherent.
- Keeps automatic TTS state in the composer waveform/Stop control and prevents message-action flashes.
- Prevents local runtime mode from booting an unrelated on-device text model.
- Preserves the mounted shell during background auth revalidation instead of flashing onboarding and rebuilding native listeners.
- Lets notifications use the actual space between the editorial header and composer, with directional overflow fades that remain correct in Android WebViews.

# Root cause

The provider gateway and visible composer had separate owners. The realtime hook was mounted in `ChatView`, but the product surface renders `ChatOverlay`, whose Talk control still invoked batch Cloud ASR. Message playback status also forced the action rail visible before Motion applied its hidden state.

For the LP3 notification regression, `HomeScreen` capped the list at an arbitrary 40% of a short viewport while the adjacent launcher region retained unused space. The shared scroll-fade fallback masked both edges unconditionally in WebViews, including the top edge at scroll start and lists with no hidden content.

# User impact

Talk now drives one continuous realtime flow from the actual composer. Transcript and response remain in the same conversation, TTS is interruptible, there is no duplicate mic, and fast turns do not flash message controls. On LP3-size screens the full available notification area is used and fades identify only content beyond the current scroll edge.
