7a:T1e25,> **Draft.** Backend, security, and behaviour work is complete and green, and the CI availability regression is fixed: fail-closed is now scoped to bridge-issued tokens (stamped with a `bridged: true` claim at /exchange re-mint), so ordinary session sync performs no datastore read at all - the pre-existing Redis-outage test passes unmodified, and a new suite proves a bridged token fails closed (503 `sso_unavailable`) during a marker-store outage. Remaining before undraft: the three surface-artifact rows (screenshots + walkthrough of the cross-origin flow), which need two live origins and are not faked here.

Security review of the dashboard/app SSO bridge found the single-use guarantee did not hold on the deployed cache and the logout marker failed open. This reworks the bridge onto a store that can actually deliver both, and closes four further findings.

## F1 (HIGH) — single-use codes were not atomic in production

The bridge claimed single-use via `cache.getAndDelete`, which on Cloudflare KV is a read-then-delete, not an atomic claim. `supportsAtomicOperations()` was never consulted, and the suite passed only because the mock was an atomic in-memory map. Two concurrent presenters of the same code could both be issued a session.

Codes now live in Postgres (`sso_bridge_codes`) and consumption is a single statement:

```sql
DELETE FROM sso_bridge_codes
 WHERE code_hash = $1 AND expires_at > now()
 RETURNING claims, challenge_hash
```

Exactly one of N concurrent presenters gets the row. Insert collision is a primary-key violation, so minting is atomically NX. Rows store `sha256(code)`, `sha256(verifier)`, and the **verified claims** — never a session JWT at rest; `/exchange` re-mints a fresh token from those claims, capped to the original token's `exp`.

This holds because KV is no longer in the path at all — the claim runs on the Worker's strongly-consistent Hyperdrive Postgres, the same store that already backs sessions and idempotency fences.

## F2 (HIGH) — logout marker failed open, and was invisible for ~60s

The marker was a cache key: a KV read miss during an outage read as "not logged out", and KV's propagation window meant a real logout stayed invisible to the paired origin. Both failure modes bridged a session that should have been dead.

The marker moves to Postgres (upsert with `GREATEST`, so it only moves forward). `isBlockedBySsoBridgeLogout` now **throws** on store failure and both bridge legs translate that into `503 sso_unavailable`, so the client falls back to per-origin login. An outage means no bridging — never "not logged out". Because codes and markers share one store, an outage that could lose a stamp also disables minting entirely.

## F3 (MEDIUM-HIGH) — dashboard sign-out never stamped, and the paired origin re-planted cookies

Three parts: both `ConsoleShell` sign-out branches now route through `signOutFromSsoBridgedHost`; `POST /api/auth/steward-session` refuses tokens issued at or before the marker with a distinct `401 session_ended`, killing the cookie re-plant server-side; and `StewardProviderRuntime` treats `session_ended` as a real revocation rather than a stale-proxy blip.

**Residual, documented in code:** the paired origin's raw bearer still works against the API until `exp`. Closing that needs a revocation lookup inside `verifyStewardTokenCached`, which is platform-wide and out of this PR's scope.

## F4/F5/F8 — binding and abuse surface

- **PKCE binding**: the app origin generates a verifier (sessionStorage only); `sha256(verifier)` travels as `challenge`. `/mint` requires it, `/exchange` requires the verifier. HTTP logs and history no longer contain enough to redeem a code.
- **Claim-then-verify**: the server consumes before checking the verifier, so every refusal path burns the code; the client also fires a verifier-less burn on state-mismatch. The mint leg requires `document.referrer` to be the paired origin, so a forced cross-site navigation cannot drive minting.
- **Origin gate**: the `Referer` fallback is removed — Origin-only, fail closed.

**F6** (plantable `steward-authed` hint) is documented as accepted risk: it is a routing hint only, loop-guarded to one bounce per tab per 5 minutes, and no unplantable cross-origin signal exists for a first visit. **F7** (logout CSRF) is pre-existing and flagged as follow-up.

## Migration

`0188_sso_bridge_store.sql` is hand-written, matching 0082–0187 in this repo (no drizzle snapshots since 0081).

81:T15e0,Closes #17527

## What this fixes

The benchmark process previously used a fixed 120-second `Promise.race`, did not abort the losing message turn, and exited without owning runtime/database shutdown. The same boot path also launched dynamic imports, plugin registration, cache warmups, maintenance DB work, and a five-second skill-command timer without a lifecycle owner. A benchmark could therefore stop reporting while work continued, or close SQL while startup jobs were still reading and writing.

This changes ownership instead of adding another deadline:

- removes the benchmark timeout option and timer race from both CLI entry points;
- passes a process-owned `AbortSignal` through the real message-service path;
- handles SIGINT/SIGTERM through cancellation plus normal shutdown rather than `process.exit()`;
- preserves partial streamed output while reporting success only for a completed, valid response;
- drains deferred imports, plugin registration, hooks, warmups, and tracked post-delivery work before adapter close;
- removes arbitrary deferred-plugin, trajectory-drain, hot-reload, and plugin-initialization timeouts;
- makes memory telemetry flush single-flight and awaited, without intercepting SIGTERM;
- removes plugin-openai's detached startup `GET /models` validation request;
- moves workbench migration, attachment backfill scheduling, and media-GC scheduling into a runtime-owned maintenance service that starts after SQL migrations;
- registers task workers before TaskService starts, then creates their idempotent queue rows only when SQL is ready;
- registers loaded skills as commands during dependency-ordered plugin initialization instead of an unowned five-second timer.

83:T3776,Closes #17044

Every authoritative Bun runtime declaration in the repository now resolves the one published canonical version from `.github/ci-bun-version.json` (`1.3.14`), and the CI contract is rewritten so no floating, mutable, implicit, divergent, or unbound declaration can come back.

## What was broken on `develop` (re-verified at `9bdcf068b` before starting)

- Root `package.json` declared `packageManager: bun@1.4.0` — **no such release exists** (npm latest: `1.3.14`), while `.github/ci-bun-version.json` and the root type anchors pinned `1.3.14`.
- `packages/feed/package.json` and `packages/elizaos/templates/project/package.json` declared the unresolvable `bun@1.4.0-canary.1` — every generated project shipped a broken toolchain declaration.
- `.github/actions/setup-bun-workspace` defaulted `bun-version` to `canary` across its **112 call sites**.
- ~30 workflow literals, ~25 `BUN_VERSION` env declarations, and one Windows matrix cell floated on `canary`; 10 `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2` refs were mutable; 2 setup-bun uses wired no version at all (the action's own default is floating `latest`); 4 `bun.sh/install` shell installs on deploy/release hosts installed `canary` or bare latest.
- `build-linux-iso.yml` resolved its Bun **at runtime from root `packageManager`** — it has been asking setup-bun for the unpublished `1.4.0` and dying at setup with the 404 that #17554's coordination comment reports. This was the one place that treated `packageManager` as the source of truth, and it is exactly the place the drift broke first.
- The existing contract guarded only its nine `GATE_WORKFLOWS` and was deliberately silent about all of the above — every one of these coexisted with a green contract run.

## What this PR does

**Commit 1 — unify every declaration (102 files).**
- Root, Feed, and generated-project-template `packageManager` → `bun@1.3.14`.
- Every floating workflow literal, env declaration, and matrix cell → the canonical pin with one uniform comment pointing at the source of truth.
- All `setup-bun@v2` refs → the reviewed commit SHA `0c5077e5…` (verified equal to the upstream `v2` tag object, and already used by the other 75 sites — behaviorally a no-op, immutably so).
- `setup-bun-workspace` default `canary` → the canonical pin (covers all 112 call sites that rely on the default).
- The two implicit `setup-bun` uses (mobile-resource-workbench) gain explicit pins; the four `bun.sh/install` lines pin `bun-v1.3.14` (deploy hosts only install when `bun` is absent, so existing hosts are untouched — no forced downgrade).
- `build-linux-iso.yml`'s runtime resolution step is replaced by the contract-enforced literal: the sync guarantee it hand-rolled (workflow ↔ packageManager) is now provided globally by the contract, without the failure mode it just demonstrated.
- Stale comments corrected everywhere they described the deleted canary tracking, the nonexistent `1.4.0`/`1.4.0-canary.1`, or contradicted the pinned value below them (`view-bundle-size`, `memperf`, `windows-ci` still said "ask for the moving canary channel"). The accurate durable comments (e.g. `cloud-cf-deploy`'s canary link-phase hang note, `release-electrobun`'s version-sensitivity warning) are kept.

**Commit 2 — rewrite the contract so this class of drift fails in repo tests.**
`packages/scripts/ci-bun-version-contract.mjs` now validates, statically, against the whole checked-in tree:
1. every `bun-version`/`BUN_VERSION` value in **workflows and composite actions** — scalar, flow-list, and block-list forms; `${{ env.BUN_VERSION }}` / `${{ matrix.bun-version }}` indirection is allowed only because the same-file declarations it resolves to are themselves validated; anything else is an **unbound expression** and fails;
2. every `oven-sh/setup-bun` ref against a reviewed-SHA set (mutable tags fail), and every use must wire an explicit version (implicit = floating `latest`, fails);
3. every `bun.sh/install` line pins `bun-v<canonical>`;
4. every `packageManager` declaring Bun equals `bun@<canonical>`; root `@types/bun`/`bun-types` anchors must equal the canonical exactly; non-root workspace type declarations are **classified advisory-only** (exact-canonical / compatible-range / drift / unparseable) per the issue's scope — they are compatibility signals, not runtime selectors;
5. a composite action's `bun-version` input default must be canonical;
6. the nine gate lanes must additionally wire the canonical literal directly (unchanged invariant, kept as defense in depth).

Deliberate floating cells (e.g. a future upstream-compat canary matrix) require an explicit file-scoped `FLOATING_ALLOWLIST` entry with a reason — **the allowlist ships empty**, so any float is a reviewable diff, can only run in addition to the pinned lane, and can never become a default or gate a release. Violations aggregate into a single run that names every stale site, which is what makes a future version bump a one-PR mechanical operation.

The full classified scan is emitted as a **machine-readable inventory** (`--inventory`), uploaded as the `bun-runtime-inventory` artifact from `test.yml` on every run — currently 435 sites: `canonical=138, reviewed-sha=85, resolvable-expression=118, exact-canonical=20, compatible-range=72, drift=2`. The two `drift` entries are the pre-existing exact `bun-types: 1.3.13` pins in `configbench`/`personality-bench`, surfaced for maintainer judgment rather than churned here (changing them would touch `bun.lock` for a non-runtime signal).

**Synthetic red tests** (`packages/scripts/__tests__/ci-bun-version-contract.test.ts`, 20 tests / 39 assertions) cover each failure mode individually: divergent concrete pin, floating gate, gate missing its pin, floating source of truth, mutable tag with a canonical version, implicit setup-bun, floating matrix cell in flow AND block form, unbound step-output expression, unpinned `bun.sh/install`, `packageManager` drift, root type-anchor drift, floating composite default — plus green-path tests for the pinned shell install, canonical composite default, allowlist passage, the range classifier, and a real-repo scan asserting zero floating/unreviewed sites remain.

## Out of scope, per the issue

Embedded Android/RISC-V Bun binary artifacts are a separate shipping boundary (`packages/app-core/scripts/bun-riscv64/` is a validated custom Rust-core build with its own device-proof record) — untouched, and deliberately not scanned by the contract.

85:T1db0,Closes #17605

`en.json` is the source catalog every other locale keys off — and it had drifted **705 keys behind source**, because the strict checker built to prevent exactly that (`packages/scripts/check-i18n.mjs`) was invoked from **no CI lane, no package script, nothing**. `defaultValue` masked every miss for English users, which is why it rotted silently; all seven non-English locales render English for those strings and could never translate them. The reverse rot accumulated too: **469 dead keys** (referenced by no literal, no source template prefix, no allowlist entry) sat in every locale, plus one key translated in all seven locales that never existed in en and is used nowhere.

## Commit 1 — catalog repair (locale JSONs only)

- **703 entries restored** to `en.json`, each value extracted **verbatim from its call site's inline `defaultValue`** (zero conflicting defaults across duplicate sites — no invented copy; byte-for-byte what English users already see). Pure line insertions: `703 insertions(+), 0 deletions(-)` on the file's existing formatting.
- **3,741 dead lines purged** across all eight locales (the 469 dead keys everywhere they existed + the seven-locale orphan `mediagalleryview.SearchActive`). Pure line removals; every file re-parsed after edit. Each deletion is checker-derived: uncovered by literals AND source template prefixes AND the allowlist.
- The 2 remaining source-missing keys (`settings.cloudOverview.localModeLabel`/`Description`) pass **runtime-conditional** defaults (ternaries on cloud-connection state). Cataloging them would freeze one branch and silently change rendered English (catalog wins over `defaultValue`), and splitting them is a `packages/ui` surface change requiring visual evidence — deliberately out of scope. They are declared, with reasons, in the new `uncatalogued` allowlist field, and the checker fails if such an entry ever outlives its call site.

## Commit 2 — make the checker wireable, then wire it

The old contract (any locale missing any key = error) made the gate permanently red — presumably why it ended up wired nowhere. New contract, aligned with what CI can hold on every PR:

- **Errors**: literal key missing from the source locale; unused source-locale key; orphaned translation (locale key absent from source); stale `uncatalogued` entry.
- **Warnings** (errors under `--strict-translations`): non-source locales missing used keys / lagging the source catalog — translation debt stays *visible* on every run without blocking unrelated PRs.
- `runI18nCheck` exported pure (no console/exit) with **10 fixture tests** covering each failure mode red and green, following the `ci-bun-version-contract` test pattern; the real-repo test asserts `ok:true` **and** that translation-gap warnings are present (a silent pass would hide the backfill the same way the unwired checker did).
- Wired into `test.yml` beside the other contracts, so no new key can ship uncataloged again.

86:T17ce,## Summary

Fixes #18054.

Anonymous navigation to `/auth/success` no longer renders a trusted "Connected" card from query parameters alone.

**Verification contract (this head `084b5512549b7d1a632dc00c8b8d786bfb199035`):**

1. Query parsing yields only a *candidate* (`resolveAuthSuccessCandidate`). Known-provider `*_connected` markers or `connection_id` alone never claim success.
2. Success requires **one** of:
   - A **callback-minted short-lived HMAC proof** verified by public `GET /api/v1/oauth/success-proof/verify?proof=…` (covers Twitter/Discord and sessionless API-key OAuth returns to `/auth/success`), and when a `connection_id` is present a sessioned browser must also own that connection; or
   - An **authenticated ownership lookup** `GET /api/v1/oauth/connections/:id` returning an active connection for the current org/user (sessioned browsers without a proof).
3. Until verification succeeds the page stays **pending**, then **verified**, **unverified**, or **unavailable** (distinct UI for transport/5xx).

**Backend changes:**

- `mintOAuthSuccessProof` / `verifyOAuthSuccessProof` (HMAC, ~10 min TTL, nonce) in cloud shared OAuth services
- Generic OAuth2, Twitter (OAuth1a + OAuth2), and Discord callbacks attach `proof` only when the redirect path is exactly `/auth/success`
- Public path allowlist for `/api/v1/oauth/success-proof/verify`
- Reserved markers (`proof`, `platform`, `connection_id`, known `*_connected`) are cleared before rewriting so a prior success URL cannot retain a valid proof across an error redirect

**Provider contracts preserved:**

| Callback | Success query shape on `/auth/success` |
| --- | --- |
| Generic OAuth2 | `{platform}_connected=true&platform=…&connection_id=…&proof=…` |
| Twitter | `twitter_connected=true&platform=twitter&proof=…` (no connection_id) |
| Discord | `discord=connected&platform=discord&discord_connected=true&proof=…` |

Forged marker-only URLs stay **unverified**.

## Security posture (mirrors certification-vast)

- `workflow_dispatch` only — no `pull_request` trigger, so PR-controlled code can never see the signing key
- both secrets exposed only to the single step that runs the chain
- `permissions: contents: read`; checkout with `persist-credentials: false`
- signing honesty is enforced by `certify:sign` itself: it refuses to sign mechanically non-pass subjects as pass, so this workflow cannot fabricate a green certification

88:T11a4,## Summary

Addresses remaining gaps from the July 23 triage of #14874.

PRs #14821 and #15084 already fixed the primary defect (model-mediated dispatch rendering). This PR closes 3 of the 5 remaining gaps identified in the triage:

### 1. Named OptimizedPromptTask slots (gap 2)
Added `scheduled_task_dispatch` and `scheduled_task_title` to the `OptimizedPromptTask` union and `OPTIMIZED_PROMPT_TASKS` array. Each dispatch surface is now independently tunable by GEPA artifacts, mirroring the existing `reminder_dispatch` precedent.

### 2. Deterministic fallback for model-free runtimes (gap 4)
The dispatch renderer previously threw a retryable `ElizaError` when `runtime.useModel` was not a function. On a stock mobile boot (no model provider), this caused every scheduled task to fail with a retryable dispatch error instead of delivering the notification.

Now, a model-free runtime receives a **neutral intensity-keyed canned message** — never the raw `promptInstructions` text. The fallback does not consult `promptInstructions` at all; it cannot leak instruction text. This preserves the acceptance criterion: "Model-free host behavior unchanged; runner unit tests still pass with zero model deps."

### 3. OptimizedPrompt slots wired into dispatch-render prompts (gap 3)
The dispatch body and title render prompts are now resolved through `resolveOptimizedPromptForRuntime(runtime, "scheduled_task_dispatch"|"scheduled_task_title", baseline)`, so offline optimizers can swap in tuned artifacts.

- `packages/core/src/services/optimized-prompt.ts` — added 2 new task slots

89:T148a,## Summary

Telegram's production poller and hosted webhook paths could lose queued updates on restart, collide platform message IDs across chats/bots, split a paired owner back into a connector-derived entity, silently swallow wire failures, or replay an outbound response after an ambiguous send.

This PR makes the vertical restart-safe:

- resolves Telegram senders against the durable canonical owner entity before any room, memory, model, or delivery side effect, and fails closed when the configured identity store is unavailable;
- centralizes owner lookup and unmatched-user fallback identity in one exported Telegram policy consumed by both full and standalone connectors, preventing cutover drift;
- keys message identity by account + chat + Telegram message ID and persists delivery state before wire egress;
- refuses replay after egress begins, reporting an explicit uncertain-delivery failure rather than risking a duplicate;
- stops dropping pending long-poll updates and enforces one process-local poller per bot token across full/standalone modes;
- scopes hosted webhook dedupe by project + bot fingerprint and writes an `egress_started` Redis barrier before Bot API delivery;
- makes connector health depend on actual poller liveness rather than service-object existence.

## Production paths

- Standard connector: `plugin-collector.ts` -> `plugin-telegram/src/index.ts` -> `service.ts` polling/supervision -> `messageManager.ts` identity, canonical ingress, audience-attested core message service, and Telegram egress.
- Standalone opt-in: `plugin-telegram-standalone/src/service.ts` -> `handler.ts`.
- Hosted webhook: `gateway-webhook/src/adapters/telegram.ts` -> `webhook-handler.ts` -> agent-server -> Bot API reply.

No media/rich-text behavior, workflow, check, deployment, or production configuration changed.

## Bidirectional proof

A production-entrypoint harness boots real `AgentRuntime` + plugin-sql/PGlite, creates a durably Telegram-bound canonical owner, drives `MessageManager.handleMessage`, verifies owner-only DM authorization and exactly one wire send, closes the runtime/database, reopens the same PGlite directory, and replays the same Telegram update. The owner row and canonical memory survive while the replay produces zero sends.

The same test copied unchanged (apart from removing the new helper-only readiness assertion/import) onto exact `origin/develop` fails because the inbound memory uses a connector-derived entity instead of the canonical owner (`inbound` is undefined).

## Verification

- Telegram real AgentRuntime/PGlite harness: 3/3 passed
- Telegram focused unit suites: 24/24 passed
- Cross-connector unmatched-user identity regression: passed in the standalone handler suite (both connectors return the same entity ID)
- Exact-head focused recheck: full connector message manager 21/21; standalone handler 3/3; both package typechecks passed
- Telegram full unit package: 120/120 tests passed; one unrelated suite could not import unbuilt `@elizaos/plugin-x402` in this borrowed dependency tree
- Standalone: 9/9 passed + typecheck passed
- Gateway webhook: 37/37 passed + typecheck passed
- Connector health: 2/2 passed
- Full Telegram plugin typecheck passed
- Biome on all changed files passed
- `git diff --check` passed
- Agent package typecheck was attempted; borrowed dependencies lack several optional plugin builds and also emit unchanged orchestrator target diagnostics. No changed health file emitted a diagnostic.

## Safety semantics

Telegram does not accept a caller idempotency key for `sendMessage`. Therefore an ambiguous network outcome cannot be safely retried. The connector writes a durable no-replay barrier immediately before egress. Success becomes `processed`/`delivered`; a crash or error after the barrier remains visible through `runtime.reportError`, logs, or webhook HTTP 503 and is never resent automatically.

# Background

- Uses acknowledged, short readiness requests that report the actual user-bus, service, curl, and health-payload states. Transient states retry; protocol failures fail immediately; only the guest-produced service-active/health-ready marker passes.
- Makes the builder cache key cover the boot hook and live-build patch.

Bug fix (non-breaking CI/release reliability and bootability change).

# Risks

**Medium.** Plugin load set and connect-handoff routing for lean-chat Calendar /
Google Workspace. Mis-gating could load Node-only Workspace on mobile or leave
owners without a working setup card. Mitigations: mobile filter last, OAuth trio
alignment, `enabled:false` final delete, trusted OAuth URL allowlist, CONFIG ids
matched to `/api/plugins`.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Makes lean-chat Google Calendar connect/sync **workable and safe**:

1. **Scheduling** — Seeded in lean-chat because Calendar is already always selected and hard-depends on it.
2. **Google Workspace (gated)** — Loads only on explicit Google signals (entries enable, configured googlechat, or full `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`+`SECRET`+`REDIRECT_URI`). Empty `{}` googlechat does **not** load. **`enabled: false` is a final deny**.
3. **Mobile order** — Companion adds run **before** the mobile allow-list so Workspace cannot re-enter iOS/Android load sets.
4. **Trusted OAuth URLs only** — Verified handoffs require known Google/Microsoft authorize hosts/paths; untrusted hosts refused.
5. **CALENDAR_SOURCES** — Verified only for allowlisted handoff states; Google → `[CONFIG:google-workspace]`; Microsoft → `[CONFIG:calendar]` with `MICROSOFT_*` pluginParameters.
6. **CONNECTOR** — Rejects calendar-feed connect phrasing; sanitized config errors; no success without trusted auth URL.
7. **PLUGIN toggle test** — regression lock for cloud self-API auth headers (runtime already on develop).

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fixes (non-breaking) + safety hardenings for lean-chat Calendar enable/connect.

### Non-claims
- Does not complete OAuth/sync without credentials + consent.
- Does not default every lean-chat agent to Workspace from the Calendar tile alone.
- Does not claim a new PLUGIN-toggle production auth fix beyond the regression test.
- Requires agent image redeploy after merge for staging.

# Documentation changes needed?

My changes do not require a change to the project documentation.

# Risks

Medium. This changes authentication caching and money-path timing for generative routes.

- Positive API-key/session decisions have a 60-second physical TTL and refresh after 30 seconds under `waitUntil`; revocation staleness is therefore bounded but non-zero.
- Flat-price media requests use the Cloudflare Durable Object admission lease before provider dispatch, with reconciliation and history persistence deferred.
- Video requests that remain pending preserve the synchronous hold needed by the late-job sweep.
- Independent rollout flags retain rollback paths for combined auth caching and the thin inference entry.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Makes warm LLM, embedding, TTS, STT, image, video, music, SFX, and prompt-generation routes perform one combined remote auth/cache decision before dispatch.
- Removes synchronous Postgres, Railway Redis, pricing-catalog, reservation-ledger, usage-history, and affiliate-payout work from covered warm Worker hot paths.
- Adds flat pricing cache support and flat Durable Object admission for media generation.
- Defers billing reconciliation and generation-history persistence with `waitUntil` after provider output is available.
- Adds a thin Worker entry that lazy-loads only the matched generative route module.
- Enables `INFERENCE_AUTH_CACHE_ENABLED` and `THIN_INFERENCE_ENTRY_ENABLED` in staging and production.
- Documents cache lifetime, cold-cache fail-closed behavior, safety exceptions, and rollback controls.

## What kind of change is this?

Performance improvement and hot-path correctness hardening.

## Why are we doing this?

Warm generative requests were paying avoidable cloud-side latency for repeated authorization/cache work and synchronous database/accounting operations. The target contract is one cache decision, no database access before provider dispatch, and minimal response-tail overhead.

# Documentation changes needed?

Documentation was updated in `packages/cloud/api/docs/inference-hot-path.md`.

8e:T125d,## Root cause and production path

Follow-up to closed #17210. Shaw's review was correct: that attempt patched `eliza-sandbox-bridge.ts`, a legacy path not used by realtime voice.

The live path is:

`voice/session/ws` → `internal-eliza-conversation-fetch` → `handleCanonicalScopedAgentStream` → `coordinateSharedStream` → `SharedRuntimeConversation` Durable Object → `SharedRuntimeChatService.stream()`.

On current `develop`, a barge-in aborts the voice session's Eliza SSE fetch. That cancels the DO response body, but `SharedRuntimeChatService.stream()` persists only after the provider's finish part. The spoken user turn and partial assistant response disappear from the shared transcript and next-turn context.

## Fix

- Finalize on consumer cancellation, provider drop, and stream failure.
- Persist the user utterance and partial reply with `interrupted: true`.
- Use stable request-derived message IDs and an idempotent/retryable finalizer, preventing duplicate assistant turns under completion/cancel races.
- Merge history by message ID rather than overwriting a whole capped snapshot.
- Make the DO durable write precede in-memory mutation.
- Serialize Postgres merge with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`.
- Annotate interrupted assistant fragments before they re-enter model context.

No work is added before first token. All added persistence is on completion/interruption paths.

## Bidirectional proof

```

```

The tests assert awaited persistence before the DO room lock releases, `interrupted:true`, stable IDs, retry after durable-write failure, no duplicate finalization, and REST transcript visibility.

8f:T15a0,## What

`app.elizacloud.ai` served the marketing site byte-for-byte — nothing in the codebase branched on the hostname, so the "app" domain was only a second name on the apex build. This adds **app-mode**: on the app hosts, an authenticated visitor lands in *their* dedicated agent instead of the marketing page.

Routing (all gated on the app hostname; the apex is untouched):

| State | Behavior |
|---|---|
| one running dedicated agent | full-page redirect into its web UI via the existing pairing-token flow |
| several running | minimal chooser, most-recently-active first |
| agents exist, none running | Instances view with a resume affordance |
| no agents | the existing "deploy your first agent" flow |
| shared-tier agents only | `chat-home` - shared agents have no per-agent subdomain to pair into, so a pairing call could not succeed |
| not signed in | the existing login flow, returning to the app entry |
| agents fetch fails | falls back to Instances — never a blank screen |

Automatic entry uses `location.replace`, not `assign`: the gate is a transient "connecting" screen, and leaving it in history let Back from the agent UI re-enter it, mint another one-time pairing token, and bounce forward — trapping the user on Firefox/Safari. An explicit chooser pick still pushes so it stays backable.

## Why

The dashboard (funds, instance management) already works end to end. The missing half of the product was the app surface actually *being* the app.

## Scope

6 files under `packages/ui/src/cloud`, +1135/-5. No codegen, no lockfile churn, no API changes — the pairing/auth contracts already existed and are reused as-is.

## Repair after review (`4e73f8dc7cc`)

- **Flag-overrides-apex is now a pinned, recorded decision**: `app-mode.test.ts` asserts `isAppModeHostname("elizacloud.ai", true) === true` with a comment pointing at the build guard as the real invariant.
- **Production builds hard-fail if a forced host-mode flag is set**: new `packages/app/scripts/forced-host-mode-guard.mjs` wired as a vite plugin - any production-mode build (all four Pages `build:web` invocations in `cloud-cf-deploy.yml`, prod and staging, console and app) throws at `configResolved` when `VITE_FORCE_APP_MODE` or `VITE_FORCE_APEX_CONSOLE` is set (loadEnv-aware, so `.env` files are covered). Dev server and `--mode development` keep the escape hatch. A misconfigured deploy now fails loudly at build time instead of silently turning the apex into a redirect gate.
- **Fixed a latent test break on the reviewed head**: the replace-instead-of-push commit stubbed only `assign`, so jsdom's unimplemented `location.replace` failed both automatic-entry pairing tests; both stubs now land in the same log, and the replace/push split is itself pinned in `app-mode.test.ts`.

- Makes capture pacing and one-shot completion/error/EOT-suppression terminal and observable.

Bug fixes and runtime improvements.

# Risks

Medium. This adds a production-facing phone gateway registration and webhook surface plus a persistent macOS relay. Primary risks are cross-user routing, leaked relay credentials, self-message loops, and stale relay processes. The implementation fails closed on identity uncertainty, persists only token digests in Cloud, uses a mode-0600 relay environment, and makes install/uninstall/status behavior deterministic and redacted.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Adds a dedicated-Mac BlueBubbles relay path for a real iPhone number. An authenticated Eliza Cloud user registers a phone gateway, receives a one-time relay credential, installs a LaunchAgent on the isolated Mac, and routes each inbound sender to that sender's linked Eliza agent. Unknown senders receive account-link onboarding. Replies return through the same registered gateway.

It also rejects messages marked `isFromMe`, the gateway's own identity, and outbound attempts targeting the gateway number before they reach Cloud or BlueBubbles.

## What kind of change is this?

Feature and safety fix across Cloud API/shared routing, app-core's local BlueBubbles bridge, the connectors UI, operator scripts, documentation, and tests.

# Documentation changes needed?

Documentation is included for registration, dedicated-Mac prerequisites, SIP/private-API requirements, install/status/doctor/uninstall lifecycle, readiness checks, and physical end-to-end acceptance evidence.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

This collapses the current GitHub Actions surface from 121 workflow files to 17 and removes 104 redundant workflows plus their orphaned scripts, tests, composite actions, and stale documentation.

The resulting model is:

- one pull-request workflow: `CI`
- one stable branch-protection context: `CI / Required`
- nightly reuse of the same CI contract, plus macOS and Windows smoke checks
- manual-only live integration, infrastructure, certification, and release operations
- path-scoped deployment and image workflows after merge
- one scheduled maintenance workflow

The PR workflow classifies changes, runs repository quality, affected tests, a focused deterministic core-shell browser smoke, and a diff-scoped secret scan. Individual diagnostic jobs remain visible but branch protection needs only the stable aggregate.

## What kind of change is this?

Infrastructure and CI simplification with narrow reliability fixes discovered while exercising the new lanes.

# Documentation changes needed?

# Risks

Low. The change adds a per-call AsyncLocalStorage scope to track whether the provider already recorded a model call, suppressing the generic fallback when so. The scope is isolated per `useModel` call via AsyncLocalStorage, so concurrent calls cannot interfere. The browser/edge sync fallback has a documented concurrency limitation (no AsyncLocalStorage), but Node (the production runtime) always uses the ALS path.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

Fixes duplicate LLM trajectory accounting (#17532). Two independent trajectory-logging paths fire for a single `useModel` call:

1. **Provider-level wire recorder**: handler → `recordLlmCall` → `logActiveTrajectoryLlmCall`
2. **Generic fallback**: `useModel` → `recordUseModelTrajectory`

Both log the same call, doubling request counts, token totals, cost, and latency attribution.

### Key design decisions

- **`markProviderRecordedCall()` centralized in `logActiveTrajectoryLlmCall`** — the single chokepoint for ALL provider trajectory logging. Both `recordLlmCall` and direct `logActiveTrajectoryLlmCall` callers (e.g. plugin-openai live streaming) mark the flag at the source.
- **`runWithModelCallRecordingScope` returns a live mutable `recordingState` reference** — not a boolean snapshot, so deferred-streaming providers (plugin-xai grok.ts) whose `recordLlmCall` resolves after stream consumption are correctly reflected.
- **Callback-stream consumption runs inside the recording scope** — the `for await` over `rawResponse.textStream` re-enters the scope per-`.next()` (with `.return()` cleanup forwarding), so provider finalizers calling `markProviderRecordedCall` find the AsyncLocalStorage store. This mirrors the pass-through `TextStreamResult` path.
- **Token/cache backfill in `recordLlmCall`** — providers that omit token counts from their detail (xAI, OpenAI buffered stream) now have missing fields backfilled from `result.usage`, never overwriting provider-supplied values. This preserves token/cost attribution when the generic fallback is suppressed.
- **Failed-attempt trajectory recording** — a rejected provider attempt now produces a trajectory entry with sanitized error metadata and `finishReason: "error"`, without fabricating an empty response or zero usage. Suppressed when the provider already logged before throwing (avoids reintroducing double-counting).
- **Pass-through `TextStreamResult` wrapping** — when `useModel` returns a raw stream (stream:true without callback), the generic trajectory record is deferred until the caller drains the stream. Each `.next()` call re-enters the recording scope via `runInModelCallRecordingScope`.
- **Browser/edge sync fallback** awaits async `fn` before restoring the store slot, with a documented concurrency limitation.
- **`createModelCallRecordingStorage` uses `process.getBuiltinModule`** instead of `require()`, matching the existing pattern in the same file.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fixes (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

99:T1a55,## What

Two onboarding convergence fixes (canon steps 1 and 3, approved by Shadow), porting proven iMessage-lane hardening to the Discord funnel. **Stacked on #17833** (base = develop, so this PR shows #17833's two commits until it merges; the new work is the single top commit).

### 1. Fail-open first contact (Discord)

`routePhoneMessage` catches a resolver throw and still sends the onboarding pitch (`reason: bridge_failed`) — a brand-new iMessage/SMS user never gets silence. `routeDiscordMessage` had no such guard: a resolver throw (DB blip, cache stampede) propagated and the first-contact DM died silently, the worst possible first impression.

Fix mirrors the phone path exactly:
- resolver throw + **DM** → loud `logger.error` (so the resolver outage still gets root-caused) then `runOnboardingChat` with the same trusted platform identity, session id, and idempotency key as the clean `unknown_owner` branch. Reply + CTA flow through unchanged.
- resolver throw + **guild** → `handled:false, reason:bridge_failed`. Guild traffic never onboards on the failure path; the login credential stays out of public channels.

### 2. Egress health (gateway-discord message POST + reply send)

Proven dropped-turn class (staging E2E 2026-08-05): the real bot **dropped a user turn on a single 401** from the fail-closed internal-JWT denylist during a Redis flake — `routeManagedAgentMessage` returned on the first `!response.ok` with no retry. The 401s are the Redis migration's flake, but the silent drop is our bug regardless.

The route is idempotent on `discord:<messageId>` (onboarding worker caches the full turn result; DO coordinator orders turns), so replaying the POST returns the identical reply instead of forking the session — bounded retry is the structurally correct fix, not a band-aid:

- New `managed-message-egress.ts`: `postManagedAgentMessageWithRetry` — up to 4 attempts, exponential backoff + jitter, retry on 401/408/429/5xx and network errors, `refreshToken()` before a 401 replay (a refresh failure doesn't abort the loop: the denylist flake heals with the same token). Deterministic 4xx (400/403/404) fail immediately.
- Reply send gets the same model (`sendReplyWithRetry`): transient failures retry (3 attempts), deterministic Discord 4xx (cannot-DM) fail fast.
- **No silent path remains**: every exhausted retry logs an explicit `...dropped after retries` error with attempt count and status.

Mirrors the bluebubbles bridge egress model (explicit pending-reply retry, never auto-drop) at the fidelity this transport allows: the POST is request/response, so retry-in-place with idempotent replay is the equivalent of "reply stays queued/retryable".

## Tests (bidirectional)

- `agent-gateway-router.test.ts` +2: resolver-throw DM fixture → greeting + CTA + `bridge_failed` (**fails on the unfixed router: 15 pass / 2 fail, proven by running the new tests against the pre-fix file**); resolver-throw guild fixture → no onboarding, no credential.
- `managed-message-egress.test.ts` (new, 11 tests): the 401-drop regression fixture (401 then success → 2 attempts, reply delivered), refresh-before-401-retry ordering, refresh-throw resilience, network-error retry, 5xx exhaustion with loud failure, deterministic-4xx fail-fast (both POST and send), first-attempt fast path, status classification.
- Full suites green: gateway-discord 26/26, cloud/shared router 17/17 + onboarding-chat 37/37. `tsc --noEmit` clean on both packages, biome clean on touched files.

9b:T9bd,## Summary

The durable cloud-pair API token (`#16666`) is written to **both** localStorage and sessionStorage by `CloudPairRelay` and re-adopted at every boot. The module `state/cloud-pair-token.ts` ships a remover, but until now no explicit user flow called it — so after an explicit **disconnect** or **agent delete**, a rotated/revoked pair key survived at rest and was re-adopted on the next launch.

This PR wires the existing purge helpers into the two explicit flows the module's own docs name (sign-out, agent deletion):

- **`handleCloudDisconnect`** (`useCloudState`) — the cleanup block already scrubs the steward JWT, the active-server token, and per-agent profile tokens; it now also calls `clearCloudPairApiToken()` (both storages) so no usable pair credential survives at rest / in memory after disconnect.
- **`deleteAgent`** (`CloudAgentsSection`) — after a successful delete (job-completed or synchronous), calls `clearStalePairCredentialsForAgent(agent.agent_id)`, which is scoped on both axes: it clears the durable pair key + active-server token only when the active server resolves to that agent, and drops only that agent's profile accessTokens. Other agents' credentials are untouched.

## Verification

- `CloudAgentsSection.test.tsx` delete suite — asserts the purge fires on job-completed and synchronous deletes and does **not** fire on failed jobs or dismissed confirmations.
- `useCloudState.backend-sign-out.test.tsx` — asserts `clearCloudPairApiToken` is called exactly once through the real disconnect path.
- Vitest: **28/28 pass** across the three touched suites (`CloudAgentsSection` 26, `useCloudState.backend-sign-out` 1, `useCloudState.cloud-sign-out` 1).
- `biome check` clean on all 4 changed files.

9c:T1a90,## Problem

Live incident (production Discord bot, trajectory `tj-69d82bb89ebb69`): asked **"how many times have i mentioned bitcoin in this channel?"**, the agent replied *"i don't see any mention of bitcoin in the recent messages i can see."* — answering a beyond-window history question from the ~20-message visible window, and denying a capability it has.

Root cause is a **false capability denial baked into the Stage-1 prompt**, which the model obeyed faithfully:

1. `createV5MessageContextObject`'s `current_turn_boundary` instruction hardcoded *"the prior_message blocks are the only window you have, and there is no separate chat-history search tool."*
2. `messageHandlerTemplate` scripted the matching canned denial for a window miss.

But the runtime **does** have that tool: the `MEMORY` action's `op:search` filters the stored `messages` record by room + query. Because Stage-1 never sees the action catalog (only the `available_contexts` list), the routing hints on that action could never reach this decision — the turn ended at Stage-1 with `contexts:["simple"]`, no `toolSearch`, no planner, no tool. The hardcoded denial also directly contradicted two of the template's own rules (`never deny a capability when a context is available`; `never simple when … "how many X"`).

## Fix

The boundary instruction now branches on the turn's **actual capability surface** — whether the role-filtered `availableContexts` (already passed by every caller) includes the `memory` context:

- **Memory context present:** state that the visible blocks are the most recent window of a longer stored conversation, and route beyond-window recall/count questions to the memory context (`requiresTool`) so the stored record is actually searched. Every anti-fabrication guarantee is retained verbatim (never claim a search a tool did not return).
- **Memory context absent:** the previous text is **byte-identical** (verified: 1161 chars, string-equal), preserving the 2026-05-25 fabricated-search guard for minimal runtimes and sub-USER roles.

Supporting: the template's canned denial defers to the ground-truth capability rule instead of dictating "no such tool", and the `memory` context catalog description names conversation recall so Stage-1 can select it. The recent-messages provider also names its window (`most recent N`) rather than presenting itself as the whole conversation.

**No user-message-text inspection anywhere** — the branch reads only the registered, role-filtered context surface. (A prose-regex intent gate was removed as a bug in #17500; this deliberately does not reintroduce that pattern.)

### Known trade (raised in adversarial review)

The gate proves *context registration*, not *action registration*: `DEFAULT_CONTEXT_DEFINITIONS` seeds `memory` in core, while the MEMORY action ships in `@elizaos/agent`. A deployment building on `AgentRuntime` with custom plugins and no memory action would get the escalating branch. Two things bound the damage: the Stage-1 catalog **already** advertises the memory context on exactly those runtimes (the boundary now merely agrees with the catalog the model already sees), and the anti-fabrication rule still forbids claiming an unrun search — so the degraded outcome is one wasted planner escalation with an honest reply, not a fabricated answer. Tightening the gate to also require a registered memory-context action is a reasonable follow-up; it would diverge the boundary from the catalog, so it belongs with catalog action-gating rather than here. Happy to make that change if preferred.

## Testing

- Two new tests in `message-runtime-stage1.test.ts` assert the rendered Stage-1 prompt for both branches; the memory-branch assertions fail on pre-fix code by construction (the removed sentence exists verbatim in develop; the new strings exist nowhere pre-fix).
- Suites green: stage1 **104**, prompts **38**, context/catalog/registry/renderer **63**, message + planner lanes **121**, provider lanes **40**. `tsgo --noEmit` clean, biome clean on all touched files.
- Adversarial review verified byte-identity of the untouched branch, all three call sites of `createV5MessageContextObject`, no prompt-cache regression (the boundary event is `stable:false`, so the KV-prewarmed stable prefix is unaffected), and that guest/stranger turns keep the old denial via role filtering.
- **Live before/after on a production Discord bot** — see evidence.

## What was broken

`resolveIdentity` in the webhook gateway threw whenever the identity resolve API answered `agentId: null`. That answer is correct — it means "known cloud account, no sandbox yet" — and the gateway was the only thing treating it as a malformed response. Because it threw instead of returning, the handler's `if (!identity)` onboarding branch was unreachable for those senders, and the throw landed in the fire-and-forget `processMessage().catch(...)` **after** the webhook had already acked 200. Telegram does not retry a 200, so the sender got silence.

Measured on production, 2026-08-05 — every linked connector identity is in exactly that state:

| platform | linked identities | of those, org owns zero sandboxes |
|---|---|---|
| telegram | 11 | **11** |
| whatsapp | 0 | 0 |
| phone (twilio + blooio) | 31 | **31** |

31 distinct organizations. The shared webhook has never worked for anyone who signed up without already owning an agent.

## What changed

**`ResolvedIdentity.agentId` is optional**, and the guard only rejects a response missing `userId`/`organizationId` — the fields whose absence really is a broken response. The `null` on the wire is normalised once, at the boundary, with no cast.

**Routing keys on "is there an agent that can serve this message"** — the sandbox row *and* its `agent:<id>:server` registry key — not on `agentId != null`. The row appears the instant provisioning starts; the key only once a container has booted and heartbeated. Branching on the row alone would answer message 1 and then go silent again until boot, permanently if provisioning ends in `error`. A per-agent webhook URL (`/webhook/:project/:platform/:agentId`) keeps precedence verbatim, including its log-and-return when no server is registered — diverting one of its senders to personal onboarding would run that flow on somebody else's bot.

The decision never reads `sandbox.status`. A stopped agent is still a resolved agent; re-onboarding one would provision a duplicate. The single line preventing that is the early return on an existing sandbox in `ensureElizaAppProvisioning`.

**An identity with no agent is not cached.** The 300s identity cache would otherwise keep serving the pre-agent answer well after the agent exists. Only settled identities are cached, which also means there is nothing to invalidate afterwards.

**The onboarding route resolves the cloud account itself** from `(platform, platformUserId)` on the internal branch — the direction `agent-gateway-router.ts` already takes for Discord. It never accepts an account named in the request body. `requireInternalAuth` is a flat shared secret with no per-service scoping (its `service` field is read by nobody), and this path reaches `launchManagedElizaAgent`, whose `launchUrl` carries a `cloudLaunchSession` redeemable **with no authentication** for the agent's bearer token at `v1/eliza/launch-sessions/[sessionId]`. A body-claimed `organizationId` would hand that to every internal-secret holder at once, including the internet-facing Railway gateway.

The provider is required rather than optional for the same reason: `resolveIdentity` without one falls back to sniffing the identifier's shape and would match a UUID, an email or a wallet address — a wider claim than "this is telegram user X", the only claim a gateway can make.

**The internal branch no longer receives `launchUrl`, `controlPanelUrl` or the transcript.** No gateway reads them — `webhook-handler.ts` reads only `body.data.reply`. The browser hook (session-authed) is unaffected and keeps the full payload.

**`|| config.agentId` is gone** from the routing expression, along with `WebhookConfig.agentId` and the `DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` lookup that fed it. It was dead by construction (it could only fire when `identity.agentId` was falsy, the case now diverted) and non-functional anyway: it holds an `agents`-table id while the registry is keyed by sandbox id, so it could never have resolved a server.

## Behaviour after the fix

Telegram or WhatsApp with a Latin display name: message 1 gets a real reply and starts provisioning; later messages keep getting honest status replies instead of silence; once the container registers, messages route to the user's own agent. Twilio and blooio need two turns by design — the display name is the phone number, so the user must actually answer "what should I call you?".

## Evidence

**Blast radius, measured before shipping** (read-only against production): 31 organizations provision a container and consume the $5 starter grant on their next inbound message. `checkAgentCreditGate` is the only brake and it only stops drained orgs. It also re-provisions anyone who deliberately deleted their agent.

**Known gate, stated rather than discovered later:** `ensureElizaAppProvisioning` runs only once a preferred name is captured, and sanitisation keeps printable ASCII only. A Telegram `first_name` that is Cyrillic, CJK or emoji-only sanitises to empty, and both name-inference patterns are ASCII — that user is asked "what should I call you?" forever unless they type a Latin-script name. Pre-existing, out of scope here, filed in the issue.

## Deploy note

This service ships via Railway, not the Worker pipeline. It needs an explicit `railway redeploy --service gateway-webhook` — a build that does not reach an already-started process is what made the Redis fix on this same service appear to fail twice on 2026-08-05.

Manual retest is also misleading for five minutes at a time: the dedup key is written before the background work with a 300s TTL, so re-sending the same text is swallowed as a duplicate. Vary the message.

[stan-cloud]


## Second round — what the review changed

An adversarial read of the first commit found three things worth fixing, all now in.

**An agent that never booted and an agent whose pod is down are not the same state, and collapsing them made the fix lie to established owners.** `agent:<id>:server` is written by a booted container and lives 30 days; `server:<name>:url` is refreshed by the pod heartbeat and expires after 120s. So a missing routing key means "never came up" — the case this PR exists for — and a present routing key with no URL means an established agent that is down or scaled to zero. The first commit sent both to onboarding, which would have answered that owner *"You're live — your private agent is running"* while the message went nowhere, and copied the onboarding transcript into their agent's memory a second time. `resolveAgentServer` now returns which of the two it found; only `unregistered` onboards.

**The gateway now sends `Idempotency-Key: <messageId>`.** The onboarding route and its session coordinator both keep a replay ledger on that header and nothing was using it. The only protection against platform redelivery was the 5-minute Redis dedup key; a retry outside that window appended the message to the transcript twice and re-entered provisioning. That existed before, but it applied to unlinked strangers only — this PR makes the onboarding path the norm for every linked-but-agentless user, so the exposure widens materially.

**`loginUrl` joins the browser-only fields.** It is built from the session-continuation token, which resolves back onto a platform session — the same class of credential as the `cloudLaunchSession` in `launchUrl`, stripped by the same argument. No gateway reads it, and when the user genuinely needs the link it is already inside `reply`.

Plus three honesty fixes: a wire type that said `agentId?: string` on the branch production actually takes, making the `null` normalisation — the one value this PR is about — invisible to the compiler; a comment of mine that claimed per-agent precedence protects senders it never reaches (a sender with no cloud account is onboarded by the branch above, per-agent URL or not, and that predates this change); and a shared JSDoc that described one caller's behaviour as the helper's contract while contradicting the other caller shipped alongside it.

Three branches the review showed were unpinned now have tests — the unreachable-pod case, the per-agent webhook whose bound agent has no server, and the identity cache write itself — plus a `resolveIdentity` suite for the narrowed guard. Thirteen pins in total, each mutation-verified.

## Found and deliberately not done here

- `packages/cloud/api/internal/webhook/config/route.ts` still returns an `agentId` that the gateway now ignores. Harmless dead payload (the caller sent that id as the query param), but it is cached into Redis for 300s. Left alone to keep this diff on the bug.
- `elizaAppConfig.defaultAgentId` (`packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/eliza-app/config.ts`) has no readers repo-wide. Already dead before this change — the gateway read the env var directly — so removing it belongs to its own sweep.
- `ensureElizaAppStarterCredits` is a read-then-write outside the org advisory lock. Two genuinely concurrent cross-session first turns are stopped from double-granting by the unique index on the deterministic credit key, but the loser throws, which surfaces as a 500 on `/onboarding/chat` and one silent message. Narrow, pre-existing, self-heals on the next message — but it is the same symptom this PR exists to remove, so it is written down rather than left to be rediscovered.

## Rebased onto develop after #17746

#17746 landed on develop first and covers part of the same journey: nullable `agentId`, the linked-but-agentless early return, and a 15s transient TTL with the 404 negative-cache write. Rebased and squashed onto `9509cb36786`; this PR is now the delta on top of it.

**What is still only here:** the `unregistered`/`unreachable` split (#17746 still log-and-returns silence for a sender whose sandbox row exists but whose container never registered — the whole boot window, and permanently on a provisioning error), `Idempotency-Key` on the onboarding POST, the API-side account resolution and response redaction, and the `DEFAULT_AGENT_ID` removal.

**Policy taken from develop, against my earlier position:** agentless and 404 identities keep the 15s transient TTL. An earlier revision of this branch cached neither, for instant cutover when the agent appears. That does not survive the clock — a container cannot boot inside 15 seconds, so the stale window costs nothing user-visible while the cache saves a resolver round trip on every inbound message from the 31 organizations this change puts through onboarding.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Replaces the sparse optional OCR expectation map with a closed discriminated policy registry covering all 63 audited slugs and all 252 slug/viewport rows.
- Adds narrow typed exemptions for one native-platform surface and four unavailable remote bundles, each with a durable reason and an observable fallback contract.
- Extracts the shared capture-case registry and adds drift tests against canonical built-in navigation and plugin view cases, so a new surface without a policy fails closed.
- Preserves remote bundle provenance in the audit report and invalidates an unregistered-bundle exemption as soon as the real bundle is captured.
- Moves the audit off the persistent self-hosted fleet and makes aesthetic/OCR failures and missing artifacts fail the workflow instead of being masked by `continue-on-error`.
- Repairs the full-page launcher clearance exposed by strict audit mode and makes the recorded mobile interaction test scroll the visible launcher viewport, asserting the final tile clears the fixed composer.
- Updates the OCR triage operator documentation.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix and test-infrastructure improvement.

# Documentation changes needed?

The operator-facing OCR triage documentation is updated in `packages/app/scripts/OCR_TRIAGE.md`. No user-facing documentation change is required.

# Risks

Medium. This changes authentication headers on protected loopback self-API calls across agent actions and three plugins. The main risks are canonical/legacy token precedence mistakes or a caller being omitted. Those are covered by shared-helper unit tests, per-fetch AST inventory enforcement, a synthetic bypass red test, and real TCP authentication tests across every named caller. No remote API, transaction, wallet, database schema, or rendered UI behavior changes.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Adds one shared `createSelfApiRequestHeaders()` resolver for the canonical `ELIZA_API_TOKEN`, legacy `ELIZA_API_AUTH_TOKEN`, alias-aware lookup, and Bearer normalization.
- Routes the protected agent, app-control, Polymarket, and Hyperliquid loopback `/api` callers through that helper instead of ad-hoc or missing auth logic.
- Adds an AST-level contract test that classifies every individual local fetch call, documents narrow non-self-API exemptions, inventories the expected protected paths, and proves a second unauthenticated fetch in the same function is rejected.
- Adds real Node TCP coverage with `ELIZA_REQUIRE_LOCAL_AUTH=1` for canonical, legacy, missing, and incorrect credentials while preserving structured caller failures.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix / security hardening (non-breaking).

# Documentation changes needed?

No project documentation change is needed. The compatibility contract and exemption rationale are executable in the shared helper tests and repository contract guard.

a1:T1911,## Problem

A "make me a tiny app" request on a live bot exposed a chain of defects that made first builds slow, leaky, or falsely failed — measured live at 192s+ with a wasted 67s retry loop, versus ~71s clean:

1. **Unwinnable creates**: fresh directory scaffolds have no runtime launcher (the worker host executes plugin exports only), so the `full` profile's launch/browser checks failed by design → every create burned its retry budget and reported "stopped" for apps that were fine.
2. **Stale deploys**: the builder's own deploy step is model-ordered; a live build (`comet-catch`) copied dist **6 seconds before its final rebuild** and shipped the scaffold placeholder while the real app sat in `dist/`.
3. **Planner-loop failure authority ate completion proofs**: `plannerToolOperationKey` keyed failures on ALL params including the free-text `description` — models re-narrate retried commands, so logically-resolved failures stayed authoritative and the terminal `APP_CREATE_DONE` REPLY was replaced with the generic fallback → verification failed on proof-missing while every check passed.
4. **Vite base-path**: the scaffold's default absolute `/assets/` paths 404 under a `/apps/<slug>/` deploy prefix (white-screened pages); the dead-sub-resource retry prompt misdiagnosed it as "missing files", so retries could never fix it.
5. **Sentinel option values**: planners emit `editTarget:"None"` (stringified absent); treating it as a real edit target sent creates down the strict edit path into a cold-registry timeout.
6. **Chat jargon**: verifier status lines ("App verification passed."), duration parentheticals, and machine proof lines reached the user.

## Fix

- New `build` verification profile (typecheck+lint+test+build) for fresh scaffolds; edits of scaffold-marked workdirs use it too; installed launchable apps keep `full`. The `build` profile **requires the structured proof** like `full` (review finding: self-reported success must not skip it).
- **Authoritative publish**: opt-in via `APP_PUBLISH_DIR`/`APP_PUBLISH_URL_BASE` settings (or `ELIZA_APP_PUBLISH_*` env) — the create prompt carries a deploy contract (relative-base build, copy, HTTP 200 + asset 200 checks, live URL in the completion), and `verifyProject` itself re-publishes the fresh dist after a pass as a recorded `publish` check. A failed copy fails the run; a stale page can no longer pass.
- `plannerToolOperationKey` excludes the free-text `description` narration param (red-green regression test pins the incident shape).
- Scaffold template ships `base: "./"`; the retry prompt names the base-path diagnosis with the exact dead URL.
- `readOptionalRefOption` filters `"None"/"null"/"undefined"` for reference-style options only (the shared `readStringOption` keeps literal `"none"` — a legitimate settings/color value; review finding).
- Chat surface: one clean ack ("Building X now — I'll post the link once it's live."), one final casual line with the live URL; pass verdicts and machine proof lines never post.

## Testing

- app-control **1628** pass + tsc clean; core failure-correlation suite **12** (incl. the new narration regression, red on old code); coordinator/sanitizer suites green on the integrated branch.
- **Live ladder on a production Discord bot** (all URLs independently probed 200): lavalamp **79s**, kaleido **97s**, snowglobe **71s**, neonpulse **65s**, comet-catch (game, real test failure caught by the verifier and fixed by the builder mid-run) **235s** — final arc is exactly two messages: ack → "your app's live: <url>". a3:T1b16,Production agent nodes have no local embedding sidecar and every agent runs on the pure cloud-embedding path. This adds the sidecar to node provisioning, surfaces its absence in node health, and self-heals nodes that lost it.

## Verified fleet state

All 8 production agent nodes were checked directly — running containers, stopped containers, pulled images, and systemd units:

| Hostname | Agent containers | Sidecar |
|---|---|---|
| eliza-prod-robot-5 | 34 healthy | none |
| eliza-prod-robot-3 | 28 healthy | none |
| eliza-prod-robot-2 | 33 healthy | none |
| eliza-prod-robot-4 | 38 healthy | none |
| eliza-prod-robot-6 | 28 healthy | none |
| eliza-core-3702b6f8 | 4 healthy | none |
| eliza-core-c5830c06 | 4 healthy | none |
| eliza-core-7226e98b | 4 healthy | none |

**Zero of 8** have a sidecar in any form. `docker inspect` across ~170 agent containers shows `ELIZAOS_CLOUD_EMBEDDING_URL=https://api.elizacloud.ai`, `EMBEDDING_DIMENSION=1536`, and no `EMBEDDING_BASE_URL`.

## Root cause

The sidecar has only ever existed as hand-installed state — **no provisioning path installs one**. Autoscaled nodes boot from `buildContainerNodeUserData` (`node-bootstrap.ts`); operator boxes come up via `onboard-docker-node.ts`. Neither mentions it, and the repo contained zero references to `text-embeddings-inference`. Two mechanisms then erase hand-installs: autoscaled nodes are rebuilt from user-data that never had it, and the disk-reclaim cycle prunes unlabelled containers. That is why this regresses after every infra churn, and why "restored on 3 nodes" does not persist.

## Change

- **New `containers/embedding-sidecar.ts`** — single source of truth: container `eliza-embedding-sidecar`, pinned `ghcr.io/huggingface/text-embeddings-inference:cpu-1.8` serving `thenlper/gte-small`, shared bridge network, loopback-only health port, model-cache bind mount, `--restart always`, and the `ai.elizaos.managed-by=eliza-cloud` label that makes it **prune-immune**. Pure builders; shell-unsafe config fails fast; all overridable via `CONTAINERS_EMBEDDING_SIDECAR_*`.
- **Bootstrap installs it** — cloud-init runs the idempotent ensure command after network setup and ghcr stale-credential cleanup (the same `denied`-pull hazard applies to this image). `onboard-docker-node.ts` gains the identical step, non-fatal.
- **Health surfaces and self-heals it** — `healthCheckNode` probes `/health` after `docker info` answers, persists the verdict to `docker_nodes.metadata.embeddingSidecar`, exposes it on `NodeCapacityReport`, ERROR-logs absence, and reinstalls with a 30-minute per-node cooldown (kill-switch `CONTAINERS_EMBEDDING_SIDECAR_SELF_HEAL=false`). The verdict never owns node status.

**The self-heal is the convergence path for the existing 8 nodes**: deploying the control plane installs sidecars fleet-wide on the next health cycle, with no hand-installs.

## Deliberately out of scope

Flipping agent containers to consume the sidecar. `applyManagedAgentInferenceEnvDefaults` pins 1536-dim cloud embeddings; a hot switch to 384-dim degrades recall until existing stores are re-embedded (#9911 class). That cutover belongs on the existing per-agent flag lane, after this lands.

a4:T112c,## Problem

The Stage-1 message prompt placed volatile provider output, especially CURRENT_TIME, before the large append-only conversation tail. Cerebras caches exact 128-token prefix blocks, so this ordering invalidated almost the entire reusable prefix every turn. The live Gemma 4 baseline reused only 41.57% of prompt tokens at p50 despite a stable system prompt.

The latency harness also summarized wall/model/provider time without preserving the exact production model input or provider-reported prompt-cache and queue timings. That made a green-looking report possible without proving what the model actually received.

## Fix

- Keep the stable system prompt first, then order the user message as current-turn boundary, chronological prior dialogue, volatile provider output, and the final current message.
- Preserve the semantic current-turn invariant without positional above/below wording.
- Capture the exact RESPONSE_HANDLER input for every warmup, sample, and cancellation invocation, including prompt segments and cache options but only allow-listed fields.
- Report prompt, cached, uncached, and cache-rate token distributions from Cerebras usage; missing cache telemetry is an explicit error rather than a fabricated zero.
- Preserve privacy-safe nested cached-token and provider time_info fields in the cloud probe.
- Give every related direct, gateway, and paired request a stable prompt_cache_key.
- Add observations only. There is no latency or cache threshold, ratchet, timeout gate, or changed-production-code test policy.

Fixes #17509

# Risks

Low, and bounded by construction. The turn body is untouched — `handleMessage` becomes a thin wrapper that registers with the registry and delegates to the unchanged implementation. The only behavioural change outside shutdown is one registry insert per turn. `stop()` gains a bounded await (10s ceiling) before teardown that previously did not exist; a hang there is impossible by construction, and the abandon path is logged, not silent.

# Background

## What does this PR do?

`DiscordService.stop()` destroyed debouncers, managers, and clients immediately, with nothing tracking in-flight `handleMessage` calls — so shutting down mid-turn tore the client out from under the turn, and the status reaction that turn had applied stayed showing "in progress" forever. Each reaction controller was a bare closure inside `handleMessage`, so shutdown had no handle to reconcile with even if it had waited.

- A turn registry (`shutdown-drain.ts`) tracks each in-flight turn and the status-reaction controller it drives.
- `stop()` awaits that drain **before** any teardown, bounded by `DISCORD_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS` (10s). No unbounded wait: blocking process shutdown indefinitely is worse than abandoning loudly.
- When the bound elapses, each still-running turn's reaction is forced to its terminal marker and the abandonment is logged with structured context (observed turns, abandoned message ids, the timeout).
- `StatusReactionController` gains `whenFinished` and `abandon()`, reusing its existing terminal transition — purely additive.

## What kind of change is this?

Bug fix (non-breaking).

## Deliberately not claimed by this PR

Naming these so #16318 does not look closed by a partial fix:

- **No inbound-ingress cordon.** discord.js keeps delivering gateway events until the client is destroyed, so a turn that *starts* after `drain()` begins is not covered. A cordon belongs to the runtime-level shutdown path, not this connector. Documented in `shutdown-drain.ts`'s header.
- **No supervisor-chain change.** `dev-ui` sends SIGKILL 1.5s after SIGTERM — shorter than any drain this plugin can offer. Making the 10s drain effective end-to-end requires a change outside `plugins/plugin-discord`.
- **No startup reconciliation** of reactions stranded by a prior hard kill.

# Documentation changes needed?

No — behaviour restored to what the connector's own contract already implied.

a8:T1522,## Summary

The `#17129` interactive Cloud login contract (`handleInteractiveCloudLogin` — a dedicated entry point that pre-opens the named popup window itself, so interactive call sites cannot omit it) is implemented on this branch together with the two test restorations it needed. Issue #17129 was still open; this PR lands both the contract and the passing tests.

Two tests in `use-first-run-conductor.test.ts` were failing against the new contract:

1. **`reaches the interactive Cloud login entry point with client auth required`** — the contract dropped the `localStorage.removeItem("steward_session_token")` guard, so a stored bearer short-circuited login entirely (the agents list is the connectivity probe). The interactive entry point is only reachable when login is genuinely needed, so the guard is restored.

2. **`closes the claimed Cloud login popup after first-run auth succeeds`** — adapted to the new contract: `handleInteractiveCloudLogin` pre-opens the named popup window itself and closes it once auth lands.

## Also

- Removed dead `preOpenWindow` / `closePreOpenedAuthWindow` plumbing from `startCloudProvisionFlow` in `use-first-run-conductor.ts`. Popup lifecycle now lives entirely inside the store's `handleInteractiveCloudLogin` entry point — the conductor no longer pre-opens or closes the auth window.
- Dropped an unrelated 53k-line regeneration of `action-search.generated.keywords.json` that had been swept into the branch; the diff is now scoped to the Cloud login contract, its call sites, and their tests (16 files, +103/−95).

aa:Tf13,## Summary

Repairs the deterministic homepage failures visible on `develop` Quality Extended run [30781438912](https://github.com/elizaOS/eliza/actions/runs/30781438912) and supersedes #17448.

- make phone readiness require the final camera frame and terminal chat texture
- make rapid platform switches generation-safe so stale replays cannot win
- expose shader render readiness and freeze reduced-motion visual state
- wait for structural onboarding-card readiness instead of fixed sleeps
- pin screenshot time, timezone, reduced motion, and one CI worker
- replace CI baseline generation/push with an exact read-only 12-file inventory
- retain Playwright failure reports and allow the real suite a 30-minute job budget
- refresh the four reviewed Linux baselines affected by the final render boundary and Geist migration

The workflow no longer grants `contents: write`, deletes baselines, commits generated pixels, or pushes from a test job.

## Root cause

The current failure has two layers. `/get-started` baselines predated the homepage font migration, producing deterministic 84%/59% diffs on every retry. Separately, the landing readiness marker was emitted by chat completion alone, before the final R3F camera projection and shader frame were guaranteed to reach the canvas. CI also ran two software-WebGL workers concurrently and could silently regenerate/push missing expectations.

This fixes the rendering boundary and the workflow policy rather than increasing screenshot tolerances or adding sleeps.

Updates `cryptography` from 48.0.1 to 50.0.0
<details>
<summary>Changelog</summary>
<p><em>Sourced from <a href="https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/blob/main/CHANGELOG.rst">cryptography's changelog</a>.</em></p>
<blockquote>
<p>50.0.0 - 2026-07-31</p>
<pre><code>
* **SECURITY ISSUE**:
  :func:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization.pkcs7.pkcs7_decrypt_der`
  and its PEM and S/MIME variants no longer expose distinguishable errors or
  timing when unwrapping a ``RecipientInfo``'s ``encryptedKey``, which could
  act as a Bleichenbacher oracle for callers that decrypt untrusted messages.
  A random key is now substituted on failure, as described in :rfc:`3218`.
  Credit to **@X1AOxiang** for reporting the issue
* Deprecated Diffie-Hellman key exchange over finite fields (FFDH).
  Everything FFDH is deprecated, including the types in
  ``cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric.dh`` and loading FFDH keys or
  parameters with the key loading APIs. Users should migrate to a more
  modern key exchange algorithm.
* Added ``xof()`` class methods to
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.SHAKE128` and
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.SHAKE256` for constructing
  algorithm instances configured for use with
  :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.XOFHash`.
* The :mod:`X.509 verification &lt;cryptography.x509.verification&gt;` APIs are now
  considered stable and are subject to our API stability policy.
* Added the :doc:`/cobblestone` recipe, an implementation of the
  Cobblestone-128 and Cobblestone-256 instantiations of the `C2SP
  chunked-encryption specification
  &lt;https://c2sp.org/chunked-encryption&gt;`_ for streaming authenticated
  encryption of large messages.
* Parsing a Signed Certificate Timestamp list now rejects encodings that
  carry trailing bytes after the list or after an individual SCT, instead of
  silently ignoring them.
* Added support for using :class:`~cryptography.x509.Name` as a field type in
  the :doc:`/hazmat/asn1/index` module.
* Loading a public key or an EC private key now rejects DER where the
  ``subjectPublicKey`` (or EC ``publicKey``) ``BIT STRING`` declares a non-zero
  number of unused bits, instead of silently ignoring it.
* Parsing a CRL entry's ``InvalidityDate`` extension now rejects a
  ``GeneralizedTime`` that carries fractional seconds or another non-DER form,
  matching the strict encoding already required for every other X.509 time
  field.
* :func:`~cryptography.x509.ocsp.load_der_ocsp_request` and
  :func:`~cryptography.x509.ocsp.load_der_ocsp_response` now reject a request
  or response whose ``version`` field is not ``v1``, the only version defined
  by RFC 6960, matching the version validation already performed when loading
  certificates, CSRs and CRLs.
* :class:`~cryptography.hazmat.primitives.hashes.XOFHash` is now supported
  when building against AWS-LC.
* HMAC (and therefore PBKDF2-HMAC) with SHA-3 hashes is now supported when
  building against AWS-LC.
* Diffie-Hellman (:doc:`/hazmat/primitives/asymmetric/dh`) is now supported
  when building against AWS-LC.
&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt; 
</code></pre>
</blockquote>
<p>... (truncated)</p>
</details>
